title.raw: 卷18 太武五王 Volume 18: Emperor Taiwu's Five Princes

sentences.zh: 晉王 東平王 臨淮王 廣陽王 南安王

translations.literal: Prince of Jin, Prince of Dongping, Prince of Linhuai, Prince of Guangyang, Prince of Nan'an
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jin, Prince of Dongping, Prince of Linhuai, Prince of Guangyang, Prince of Nan'an

sentences.zh: 東平王翰，真君三年封秦王，拜侍中、中軍大將軍，參典都曹事。

translations.literal: Prince Han of Dongping was enfeoffed as Prince of Qin in the third year of Zhenjun, appointed Attendant-in-Chief and Grand General of the Central Army, and took part in overseeing the affairs of the Capital Offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenjun, Prince Han of Dongping was enfeoffed as Prince of Qin and appointed Attendant-in-Chief and Grand General of the Central Army, with a role in the administration of the capital offices.

sentences.zh: 忠貞雅正，百僚憚之。

translations.literal: He was loyal, upright, and refined; the hundred officials stood in awe of him.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal, upright, and refined, he commanded the respect of the entire court.

sentences.zh: 太傅高允以翰年少，作諸侯箴以遺之，翰覽之大悅。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Gao Yun, considering Han's youth, composed an admonition for feudal lords and presented it to him; Han read it and was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Because Han was still young, Grand Tutor Gao Yun wrote an admonition for feudal lords and sent it to him; Han read it with great delight.

sentences.zh: 後鎮枹罕，以信惠撫眾，羌戎敬服。

translations.literal: Later he was stationed at Fuhan, where with trust and kindness he soothed the people, and the Qiang and Rong submitted in respect.
translations.idiomatic: Later he garrisoned Fuhan, winning the people through trust and kindness until the Qiang and Rong looked up to him in submission.

sentences.zh: 改封東平王。

translations.literal: His title was changed to Prince of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: He was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 世祖崩，諸大臣等議欲立翰，而中常侍宗愛與翰不協，矯太后令立南安王余，遂殺翰。

translations.literal: When Shizu died, the chief ministers deliberated on installing Han, but the palace attendant Zong Ai, who was at odds with Han, forged an order from the empress dowager to install Prince Yu of Nan'an, and then had Han killed.
translations.idiomatic: After Shizu's death the chief ministers wished to enthrone Han, but the palace attendant Zong Ai, who was at odds with him, forged an empress dowager's order to install Prince Yu of Nan'an instead, and then had Han killed.

sentences.zh: 子道符，襲爵，中軍大將軍。

translations.literal: His son Daofu succeeded to the title and served as Grand General of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: His son Daofu inherited the title and was appointed Grand General of the Central Army.

sentences.zh: 顯祖踐阼，拜長安鎮都大將。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzu ascended the throne, he was appointed Grand General of the Chang'an Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzu took the throne, he was appointed Grand General of the Chang'an Garrison.

sentences.zh: 皇興元年，謀反，司馬段太陽討斬之，傳首京師。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangxing he plotted rebellion; the marshal Duan Taiyang defeated and beheaded him, and his head was sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Huangxing he rose in rebellion; Marshal Duan Taiyang defeated and executed him, and his head was sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 子提，襲。

translations.literal: His son Ti succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ti inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 為梁州刺史，以貪縱削除，加罰，徙配北鎮。

translations.literal: As Inspector of Liang Province he was removed from office for greed and license, punished further, and exiled to serve in the northern garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as Inspector of Liang Province he was stripped of office for greed and excess, punished further, and sent to the northern garrisons in exile.

sentences.zh: 久之，提子員外郎穎免冠請解所居官，代父邊戍，高祖不許。

translations.literal: After a long time, Ti's son Ying, an acting gentleman of the palace, removed his cap and requested to resign his own post and take his father's place on the frontier; Emperor Gaozu did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Years later Ti's son Ying, an acting gentleman of the palace, removed his official cap and asked to resign his post and take his father's place on the frontier; Emperor Gaozu refused.

sentences.zh: 後詔提從駕南伐，至洛陽，參定遷都之議。

translations.literal: Later an edict ordered Ti to accompany the emperor on the southern campaign; when they reached Luoyang he took part in deliberations on moving the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Later an edict summoned Ti to accompany the emperor on the southern campaign; at Luoyang he joined in deliberations on moving the capital.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 以預參遷都功，追封長鄉縣侯。

translations.literal: Because of his share in the work of moving the capital, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Changxiang County.
translations.idiomatic: For his part in the deliberations on moving the capital, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Changxiang County.

sentences.zh: 世宗時，贈雍州刺史，諡曰懿。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Shizong he was posthumously given the office of Inspector of Yong Province and the posthumous title Magnificent.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Shizong he was posthumously appointed Inspector of Yong Province and given the posthumous title Magnificent.

sentences.zh: 子彧，字文若，紹封。

translations.literal: His son Yu, styled Wenruo, succeeded to the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yu, styled Wenruo, inherited the enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 彧少有才學，時譽甚美。

translations.literal: Yu from youth had talent and learning, and his contemporary reputation was very fine.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Yu showed talent and learning, and his reputation among contemporaries was excellent.

sentences.zh: 侍中崔光見彧，退而謂人曰：「黑頭三公，當此人也。」

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Chief Cui Guang saw Yu and, on leaving, said to others: "The dark-haired man who will reach the three highest offices — it will be this one."
translations.idiomatic: When Attendant-in-Chief Cui Guang met Yu, he withdrew and told others, "The dark-haired man destined for the three highest offices — that will be this one."

sentences.zh: 少與從兄安豐王延明、中山王熙並以宗室博古文學齊名，時人莫能定其優劣。

translations.literal: From youth he and his cousins Prince Yanming of Anfeng and Prince Xi of Zhongshan were alike famed among the imperial clan for classical learning and letters, and men of the time could not settle which was superior.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he and his cousins Prince Yanming of Anfeng and Prince Xi of Zhongshan were equally renowned among the imperial clan for classical learning and letters, and contemporaries could not agree which was the better.

sentences.zh: 尚書郎范陽盧道將謂吏部清河崔休曰：「三人才學雖無優劣，然安豐少於造次，中山皂白太多，未若濟南風流沉雅。

translations.literal: Langzhong of the Secretariat Lu Daojiang of Fanyang said to Cui Xiu of the Ministry of Personnel in Qinghe: "The three men's talent and learning are not unequal, yet Anfeng is too quick in haste, Zhongshan has too much black and white, and neither matches Jinan's refined and grave elegance.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Daojiang of Fanyang, a gentleman of the Secretariat, told Cui Xiu of the Ministry of Personnel in Qinghe: "Though the three are matched in talent, Anfeng is too rash in a pinch, Zhongshan argues black and white too much, and neither equals Jinan's cultivated, grave elegance.

sentences.zh: 」時人為之語曰：「三王楚琳琅，[7]未若濟南備圓方。

translations.literal: " Men of the time made a saying of it: "The three princes are Chu's fine jades, [7] yet none matches Jinan's roundness and squareness complete.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time composed a saying: "The three princes are jewels of Chu, [7] yet none is as complete in roundness and squareness as Jinan."

sentences.zh: 」彧姿制閑裕，吐發流靡，琅邪王誦有名人也，見之未嘗不心醉忘疲。

translations.literal: " Yu's bearing was easy and ample, his speech flowing and graceful; Wang Song of Langye was a man of reputation, and whenever he saw Yu he could not but be heart-struck and forget fatigue.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's bearing was relaxed and ample, his speech fluent and graceful. Wang Song of Langye was a man of note, and whenever he met Yu he was so captivated that he forgot his weariness.

sentences.zh: 拜前軍將軍、中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed General of the Van and Gentleman Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General of the Van and Gentleman Attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 奏郊廟歌辭，時稱其美。

translations.literal: He presented hymns for the suburban and ancestral temples, and men of the time praised their beauty.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted hymns for the suburban and ancestral rites, which contemporaries praised.

sentences.zh: 除給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 彧本名亮，字仕明，時侍中穆紹與彧同署，避紹父諱，啟求改名。

translations.literal: Yu's original name was Liang, styled Shiming; at the time Attendant-in-Chief Mu Shao served in the same office as Yu, and to avoid the taboo on Shao's father's name he submitted a request to change his name.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had originally been named Liang, styled Shiming. Attendant-in-Chief Mu Shao then served in the same office, and to avoid the taboo on Shao's father's name Yu petitioned to change his name.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「仕明風神運吐，常自以比荀文若，可名彧，以取定體相倫之美。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Shiming's spirit and bearing are lofty in expression; he often compares himself to Xun Yu. He may be named Yu, to take the beauty of matching that fixed stature and peer."
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "Shiming's spirit and bearing are lofty; he often compares himself to Xun Yu. Let him be named Yu, to reflect the honor of matching that fixed stature and peer."

sentences.zh: 」彧求復本封，詔許，復封臨淮，寄食相州魏郡。

translations.literal: " Yu requested restoration of his original enfeoffment; the edict assented, and he was again enfeoffed at Linhuai, with sustenance drawn from Wei Commandery in Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yu asked to recover his original enfeoffment; the court assented and re-enfeoffed him at Linhuai, with sustenance drawn from Wei Commandery in Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 又長兼御史中尉，彧以為倫敍得之，不謝。

translations.literal: He was also made acting Imperial Censor; Yu thought the order of rank fitting and did not decline.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made acting Imperial Censor; Yu thought the appointment suited the order of rank and did not decline.

sentences.zh: 領軍于忠忿，言之朝廷曰：「臨淮雖復風流可觀，而無骨鯁之操，中尉之任，恐非所堪。

translations.literal: Commander of the Guards Yu Zhong was angered and said to the court: "Though Linhuai is again pleasing in manner, he lacks the fiber of unbending integrity; the post of Imperial Censor, I fear, is not what he can bear.
translations.idiomatic: Commander of the Guards Yu Zhong was incensed and told the court: "Linhuai may be pleasing in manner, but he lacks unbending fiber; I doubt he can bear the office of Imperial Censor."

sentences.zh: 」遂去威儀，單車而還，朝流為之歎息。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he removed his insignia of office and returned in a single cart; the court currents sighed over it.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon set aside his insignia and returned alone in a single cart, to the regret of court opinion.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍中、衞將軍、左光祿大夫、兼尚書左僕射，攝選。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Attendant-in-Chief, General of the Guard, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness on the Left, and Acting Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, with charge of selection.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through Attendant-in-Chief, General of the Guard, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness on the Left, and Acting Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, with charge of official selection.

sentences.zh: 是時，蕭衍遣將圍逼溫湯，進彧以本官為東道行臺。

translations.literal: At that time Xiao Yan sent generals to press the siege of Wentang; Yu was advanced in his existing office to Eastern Route Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xiao Yan sent generals to press the siege of Wentang, and Yu was advanced in his existing office to Eastern Route Commissioner.

sentences.zh: [8]會尒朱榮入洛，殺害元氏。

translations.literal: [8] It happened that Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang and slaughtered the Yuan clan.
translations.idiomatic: [8] Just then Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang and slaughtered the Yuan clan.

sentences.zh: 彧撫膺慟哭，遂奔蕭衍。

translations.literal: Yu beat his breast and wept bitterly, then fled to Xiao Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu beat his breast and wept bitterly, then fled to Xiao Yan.

sentences.zh: 衍遣其舍人陳建孫迎接，并觀彧為人。

translations.literal: Yan sent his house attendant Chen Jiansun to welcome him and also to observe Yu's character.
translations.idiomatic: Yan sent his house attendant Chen Jiansun to welcome him and to observe his character.

sentences.zh: 建孫還報，稱彧風神閑儁。

translations.literal: Jiansun returned and reported that Yu's spirit and bearing were easy and distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Jiansun returned and reported that Yu's spirit and bearing were easy and distinguished.

sentences.zh: 衍亦先聞名，深相器待，見彧於樂遊園，因設宴樂。

translations.literal: Yan had also heard his name before and greatly valued him; he received Yu at the Park of Joyful Excursions and there set out a banquet with music.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had already heard of him and held him in high regard; he received Yu at the Park of Joyful Excursions and set out a banquet with music.

sentences.zh: 彧聞樂聲，歔欷，涕淚交下，悲感傍人，衍為之不樂。

translations.literal: When Yu heard the music he sighed and wept, tears streaming down; his grief moved those beside him, and Yan himself was displeased on his account.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu heard the music he sighed and wept until tears streamed down, moving those beside him; Yan himself was cast down on his account.

sentences.zh: 自前後奔叛，皆希旨稱魏為偽，唯彧上表啟，常云魏臨淮王。

translations.literal: From earlier and later, those who fled in defection all toadied and called Wei false; only Yu in memorials and reports always said Prince Yu of Linhuai of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Before and after, defectors flattered Yan by calling Wei a false state; only Yu in memorials and reports always styled himself Prince Yu of Linhuai of Wei.

sentences.zh: 衍體彧雅性，不以為責。

translations.literal: Yan understood Yu's refined nature and did not blame him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan understood Yu's refined character and did not reproach him.

sentences.zh: 及知莊帝踐阼，彧以母老請還，辭旨懇切。

translations.literal: When he learned that Emperor Zhuang had ascended the throne, Yu, because his mother was old, requested to return; his words were earnest in tone.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that Emperor Zhuang had taken the throne, Yu asked to return because his mother was old; his plea was deeply earnest.

sentences.zh: 衍惜其人才，又難違其意，遣其僕射徐勉私勸彧曰：「昔王陵在漢，姜維相蜀，在所成名，何必本土。

translations.literal: Yan prized his talent yet found it hard to go against his wish; he sent his Vice Director Xu Mian privately to urge Yu, saying: "In former times Wang Ling served Han and Jiang Wei served Shu; each won fame where he stood — why must it be one's native land?
translations.idiomatic: Yan prized his talent yet could not easily refuse his wish; he sent Vice Director Xu Mian privately to urge Yu: "Wang Ling once served Han and Jiang Wei served Shu; each won fame where he stood — why must it be one's native soil?"

sentences.zh: 」彧曰：「死猶願北，況於生也。

translations.literal: " Yu said: "Even in death I would wish to face north; how much more while living.
translations.idiomatic: Yu replied: "Even in death I would wish to face north; how much more while I still live."

sentences.zh: 」衍乃以禮遣。

translations.literal: " Yan then sent him away with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Yan then sent him away with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 彧性至孝，事父母盡禮，自經違離，不進酒肉，容貌憔悴，見者傷之。

translations.literal: Yu's nature was utmost in filial piety; in serving his parents he observed every rite. From the time he was separated from them he took no wine or meat; his appearance grew haggard, and those who saw him were moved.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was utterly filial and served his parents with every observance. From the time he was parted from them he took no wine or meat; his face grew haggard, and those who saw him were moved.

sentences.zh: 累除位尚書令、大司馬、兼錄尚書。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly appointed Minister of the Secretariat, Grand Marshal, and concurrently Recorder of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly appointed Minister of the Secretariat, Grand Marshal, and concurrently Recorder of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 莊帝追崇武宣王為文穆皇帝，廟號肅祖，母李妃為文穆皇后，將遷神主於太廟，以高祖為伯考。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang posthumously honored Prince Wuxuan as Emperor Wenmu, with temple name Suzu; his mother Consort Li as Empress Wenmu; the spirit tablets were to be moved to the Grand Temple, with Emperor Gaozu as elder paternal ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang posthumously honored Prince Wuxuan as Emperor Wenmu, with temple name Suzu, and his mother Consort Li as Empress Wenmu; their spirit tablets were to enter the Grand Temple, with Emperor Gaozu styled elder paternal ancestor.

sentences.zh: 彧表諫曰：「漢祖創業，香街有太上之廟；

translations.literal: Yu memorialized in remonstrance, saying: "When Han's founder founded the enterprise, Xiang Street had a temple to the Supreme Emperor;
translations.idiomatic: Yu submitted a memorial of remonstrance: "When Han's founder founded the dynasty, Xiang Street had a temple to the Supreme Emperor;

sentences.zh: 光武中興，南頓立舂陵之寢。

translations.literal: when Guangwu restored the line, Nandun established the lodge of Chunling.
translations.idiomatic: when Guangwu restored the line, Nandun established the lodge of Chunling.

sentences.zh: 元帝之於光武，疏為絕服，猶尚身奉子道，入繼大宗。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan toward Guangwu was distant enough for severed mourning, yet he still personally observed the son's way and entered to continue the great lineage.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan toward Guangwu was distant enough for severed mourning, yet he still personally observed the son's way and entered to continue the great lineage.

sentences.zh: 高祖之於聖躬，親實猶子。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu toward Your Majesty's person was in fact as close as son.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu toward Your Majesty was in fact as close as a son.

sentences.zh: 陛下既纂洪緒，豈宜加伯考之名？

translations.literal: Your Majesty has already succeeded to the great succession — how can it be fitting to add the name of elder paternal ancestor?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has already succeeded to the great succession — how can it be fitting to add the name of elder paternal ancestor?

sentences.zh: 且漢宣之繼孝昭，斯乃上後叔祖，豈忘宗承考妣，蓋以大義斯奪。

translations.literal: Moreover, when Han Xuandi succeeded Xiaozhao, that was to follow after a great-uncle — how could he forget the ancestors he continued from father and mother? It was because great principle overrode it.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Xuandi succeeded Xiaozhao, he followed a great-uncle — yet he did not forget the ancestors from whom he continued; great principle overrode the bond.

sentences.zh: 及金德將興，宣王受寄，自茲而降，世秉威權。

translations.literal: When the virtue of Metal was about to rise, the King of Xuan received the mandate; from that time down, the world held to power.
translations.idiomatic: When the virtue of Metal was about to rise, the King of Xuan received the mandate; from that time on, his line held power generation after generation.

sentences.zh: 景王意存毀冕，文王心規裂冠，雖祭則魏主，而權歸晉室，昆之與季，實傾曹氏。

translations.literal: The King of Jing harbored intent to destroy the regalia; the King of Wen in heart plotted to split the crown. Though they sacrificed to the Wei ruler, power returned to the Jin house; Kun and Ji in fact overturned the Cao clan.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Jing harbored intent to destroy the regalia; the King of Wen in heart plotted to split the crown. Though sacrifice was offered to the Wei ruler, power returned to Jin; Kun and Ji in fact overturned the house of Cao.

sentences.zh: 且子元，宣王冢胤，文王成其大業。

translations.literal: Moreover Ziyuan was the direct heir of the King of Xuan; the King of Wen completed his great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Ziyuan was the direct heir of the King of Xuan, and the King of Wen completed his great enterprise.

sentences.zh: 故晉武繼文祖宣，景王有伯考之稱。

translations.literal: Thus Jin Wu continued Wen and honored Xuan as ancestor; the King of Jing had the title of elder paternal ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Jin Wu continued Wen and honored Xuan as ancestor, and the King of Jing bore the title of elder paternal ancestor.

sentences.zh: 以今類古，恐或非儔。

translations.literal: To class the present with antiquity — I fear it may not be a match.
translations.idiomatic: To class the present with antiquity — I fear it may not be a true parallel.

sentences.zh: 又臣子一例，義彰舊典，禘祫失序，著譏前經。

translations.literal: Again, minister and ruler are one pattern; the meaning shines in old canons; disorder in di and xia sacrifices is censured in former classics.
translations.idiomatic: Minister and ruler share one pattern, and the meaning shines in old canons; disorder in di and xia sacrifices is censured in the classics.

sentences.zh: 高祖德溢寰中，道超無外。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu's virtue overflowed within the four seas; his Way surpassed all beyond.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu's virtue filled the realm; his Way surpassed all beyond.

sentences.zh: 肅祖雖勳格宇宙，猶曾奉贄稱臣。

translations.literal: Though Suzu's merit matched the cosmos, he had once presented tribute and called himself minister.
translations.idiomatic: Though Suzu's merit matched the cosmos, he had once presented tribute and styled himself a minister.

sentences.zh: 穆皇后稟德坤元，復將配享乾位，此乃君臣並筵，嫂叔同室，歷觀墳籍，未有其事。」

translations.literal: Empress Wenmu embodied the virtue of the earthly principle, yet was again to be paired in sacrifice on the seat of Heaven — this is ruler and minister at one mat, sister-in-law and brother-in-law in one chamber; searching through the tomes, there is no such thing."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wenmu embodied the virtue of the earthly principle, yet was again to share sacrifice on Heaven's seat — ruler and minister at one mat, sister-in-law and brother-in-law in one chamber; in all the tomes there is no precedent for this."

sentences.zh: 時莊帝意銳，朝臣無敢言者，唯彧與吏部尚書李神儁並有表聞。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Zhuang's intent was sharp, and no courtier dared speak; only Yu and Li Shenjun, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, also submitted memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang's mind was set, and no courtier dared speak; only Yu and Li Shenjun, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, also submitted memorials.

sentences.zh: 詔報曰：「文穆皇帝勳格四表，道邁百王，是用考循舊軌，恭上尊號。

translations.literal: The edict in reply said: "Emperor Wenmu's merit matched the four quarters and his Way surpassed the hundred kings; therefore we followed the old track in reverence and raised the honored title.
translations.idiomatic: The reply edict said: "Emperor Wenmu's merit matched the four quarters and his Way surpassed the hundred kings; therefore we followed the old track and raised the honored title.

sentences.zh: 王表云漢太上於香街，南頓於舂陵。

translations.literal: Your memorial says that Han's Supreme Emperor was at Xiang Street and Nandun at Chunling.
translations.idiomatic: Your memorial says Han's Supreme Emperor was at Xiang Street and Nandun at Chunling.

sentences.zh: 漢高不因瓜瓞之緒，光武又無世及之德，皆身受符命，不由父祖，別廟異寢，於理何差？

translations.literal: Han Gao did not rely on melon-and-vine succession; Guangwu likewise had no virtue of succession through generations — both personally received the mandate, not through father or grandfather; separate temples and separate lodges — wherein lies the difference in principle?
translations.idiomatic: Han Gao did not rely on collateral succession; Guangwu had no virtue of generation upon generation — both personally received the mandate, not through father or grandfather. Separate temples and lodges — wherein lies the difference in principle?

sentences.zh: 文穆皇帝天眷人宅，歷數有歸，朕忝承下武，遂主神器，既帝業有統，漢氏非倫。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenmu was favored by Heaven and dwelt among men; the succession had its return; I am shamed to continue the martial line and so hold the sacred vessel; since the imperial line has its succession, Han is not the parallel.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenmu was favored by Heaven; the succession had its return. I am shamed to continue the martial line and hold the sacred vessel; since the imperial line has its succession, Han is not the parallel.

sentences.zh: 若以昔況今，不當移寢，則魏太祖、晉景帝雖王跡已顯，皆以人臣而終，豈得與餘帝別廟，有闕餘序。

translations.literal: If, comparing past with present, the lodge should not be moved, then Wei Taizu and Jin Jingdi, though kingly traces were already clear, both ended as subjects — can they be given separate temples apart from the rest, with the sequence incomplete?
translations.idiomatic: If past is compared with present and the lodge should not be moved, then Wei Taizu and Jin Jingdi, though kingly traces were clear, both ended as subjects — can they have separate temples while the sequence remains incomplete?

sentences.zh: [9]漢郡國立廟者，欲尊高祖之德，使饗遍天下，非關太廟神主，獨在外祠薦。

translations.literal: [9] Where Han commanderies and kingdoms established temples, it was to honor Gaozu's virtue and spread offerings throughout the realm — it does not concern the spirit tablets of the Grand Temple alone being offered to outside shrines.
translations.idiomatic: [9] Where Han commanderies and kingdoms established temples, it was to honor Gaozu's virtue and spread offerings throughout the realm — not to set Grand Temple spirit tablets apart in outside shrines.

sentences.zh: 漢宣之父，亦非勳德所出，雖不追尊，不亦可乎？

translations.literal: The father of Han Xuandi likewise did not issue from merit and virtue; though he was not posthumously honored, would that not also be permissible?
translations.idiomatic: The father of Han Xuandi likewise did not issue from merit and virtue; though he was not posthumously honored, would that not also be permissible?

sentences.zh: 伯考之名，自是尊卑之稱，何必準古而言非類也。

translations.literal: The name of elder paternal ancestor is itself a term of honor and humility — why must one take antiquity as standard and say it is not of a kind?
translations.idiomatic: The name of elder paternal ancestor is itself a term of rank — why must antiquity be the standard and call it unlike?

sentences.zh: 復云君臣同列，嫂叔共室，當以文穆皇帝昔遂臣道，以此為疑。

translations.literal: Again you say ruler and minister in the same row and sister-in-law and brother-in-law in one chamber — this takes the fact that Emperor Wenmu once followed the way of a subject as the ground of doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Again you say ruler and minister in the same row and sister-in-law and brother-in-law in one chamber — you take the fact that Emperor Wenmu once followed the way of a subject as ground for doubt.

sentences.zh: 禮：『天子元子猶士。

translations.literal: The Rites say: "The eldest son of Heaven is still like a commoner."
translations.idiomatic: The Rites say: "The eldest son of Heaven is still like a commoner."

sentences.zh: 』禘祫豈不得同室乎？

translations.literal: " Can di and xia sacrifices not share one chamber?
translations.idiomatic: Can di and xia sacrifices not share one chamber?

sentences.zh: 且晉文、景共為一代，議者云，世限七，主無定數。

translations.literal: Moreover Jin Wen and Jin Jing were of one generation; debaters said the world limit is seven, with no fixed number of lords.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Wen and Jin Jing were of one generation; debaters said the limit is seven generations, with no fixed number of lords.

sentences.zh: 昭穆既同，明有共室之理。

translations.literal: Since zhao and mu are the same, clearly there is reason for a shared chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Since zhao and mu are aligned, clearly there is reason for a shared chamber.

sentences.zh: 禮既有祔，嫂叔何嫌。

translations.literal: Where the Rites provide for fu, what doubt is there of sister-in-law and brother-in-law?
translations.idiomatic: Where the Rites provide for fu, what doubt is there of sister-in-law and brother-in-law?

sentences.zh: 禮，士祖禰一廟，豈無婦舅共室也？

translations.literal: The Rites say that a commoner has one temple for ancestor and father — is there not also wife's uncle in one chamber?
translations.idiomatic: The Rites say a commoner has one temple for ancestor and father — is there not also wife's uncle in one chamber?

sentences.zh: 若專以共室為疑，容可更議遷毀。

translations.literal: If you take shared chamber alone as doubt, it may be discussed again whether to move or destroy.
translations.idiomatic: If shared chamber alone is doubt, it may be discussed again whether to move or destroy.

sentences.zh: 」莊帝既逼諸妹之請，此辭意黃門侍郎常景、中書侍郎邢子才所替成也。

translations.literal: " Emperor Zhuang, pressed by his sisters' pleas, had this reply drafted by Gentleman Attendant of the Yellow Gate Chang Jing and Gentleman Attendant of the Secretariat Xing Zicai.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang, pressed by his sisters' pleas, had this reply drafted by Gentleman Attendant of the Yellow Gate Chang Jing and Gentleman Attendant of the Secretariat Xing Zicai.

sentences.zh: 又追尊兄彭城王為孝宣皇帝，彧又面諫曰：「陛下中興，意欲憲章前古，作而不法，後世何觀？

translations.literal: He also posthumously honored his elder brother Prince Pengcheng as Emperor Xiaoxuan; Yu again remonstrated to his face, saying: "Your Majesty in restoring the line wishes to take former antiquity as model — to act without following the law, what will later ages see?
translations.idiomatic: He also posthumously honored his elder brother Prince Pengcheng as Emperor Xiaoxuan; Yu again remonstrated face to face: "Your Majesty in restoring the line wishes to take antiquity as model — to act without law, what will later ages see?

sentences.zh: 歷尋書籍，未有其事。

translations.literal: Searching through books and records, there is no such thing.
translations.idiomatic: Searching books and records, there is no precedent.

sentences.zh: 願割友于之情，使名器無爽。

translations.literal: I beg you to cut the feeling between friends and brothers, so that titles and offices suffer no harm.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to set aside brotherly feeling so that titles and offices suffer no harm.

sentences.zh: 」帝不從。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not assent.

sentences.zh: 及神主入廟，復敕百官悉陪從，一依乘輿之式。

translations.literal: When the spirit tablets entered the temple, he again ordered all officials to accompany them, entirely according to the imperial carriage form.
translations.idiomatic: When the spirit tablets entered the temple, he again ordered all officials to accompany them in the full form reserved for the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 彧上表，以為爰自中古，迄於下葉，崇尚君親，褒明功懿，乃有皇號，終無帝名。

translations.literal: Yu submitted a memorial, holding that from middle antiquity down to later ages, in honoring ruler and kin and making clear merit and virtue, there were honored titles but in the end no imperial names.
translations.idiomatic: Yu submitted a memorial holding that from middle antiquity down, in honoring ruler and kin and making merit clear, there were honored titles but never imperial names.

sentences.zh: 今若去帝，直留皇名，求之古義，少有依準。

translations.literal: If now the word emperor is removed and only the honored name left, sought in ancient meaning there is little to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: If the word emperor is removed and only the honored name left, little in ancient meaning supports it.

sentences.zh: 又不納。

translations.literal: Again he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Again he did not accept.

sentences.zh: 尒朱榮死，除彧司徒公。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong died, Yu was appointed Duke of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong died, Yu was appointed Duke of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 尒朱世隆率部北叛，詔彧防河陰。

translations.literal: Erzhu Shilong led his division in rebellion to the north; an edict ordered Yu to guard Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Shilong led his division in rebellion to the north; an edict ordered Yu to guard Heyin.

sentences.zh: 及尒朱兆率眾奄至，彧出東掖門，為賊所獲。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Zhao led his masses in a sudden arrival, Yu went out the eastern side gate and was seized by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao led his forces in a sudden arrival, Yu went out the eastern side gate and was seized by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 見兆，辭色不屈，為羣胡所毆薨。

translations.literal: Seeing Zhao, his words and color did not bend; he was beaten to death by the barbarian horde.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Zhao, he would not bend in word or color; the barbarian horde beat him to death.

sentences.zh: 出帝贈太師、太尉公、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Emperor Chu posthumously gave him Grand Preceptor, Duke of the Grand Commandant, and Inspector of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Chu posthumously appointed him Grand Preceptor, Duke of the Grand Commandant, and Inspector of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 彧美風韻，善進止，衣冠之下，雅有容則。

translations.literal: Yu had fine bearing and grace, skilled in deportment; beneath cap and gown he had an elegant presence.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had fine bearing and grace and skilled deportment; beneath cap and gown he showed an elegant presence.

sentences.zh: 博覽羣書，不為章句。

translations.literal: He broadly read the classics but did not compose chapter-and-verse commentary.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely in the classics but did not compose chapter-and-verse commentary.

sentences.zh: 所著文藻雖多亡失，猶有傳於世者。

translations.literal: Though much of his literary work was lost, some still circulates in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Though much of his literary work was lost, some still circulates.

sentences.zh: 然居官不能清白，所進舉止於親婭，為識者所譏。

translations.literal: Yet in office he could not keep himself pure; his promotions and recommendations stopped at kin by marriage, and men of discernment ridiculed him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in office he could not keep himself pure; his promotions and recommendations favored kin by marriage, and discerning men ridiculed him for it.

sentences.zh: 無子。

translations.literal: He had no son.
translations.idiomatic: He left no son.

sentences.zh: 弟孝友，少有時譽，襲爵淮陽王，累遷滄州刺史。

translations.literal: His younger brother Xiaoyou, from youth enjoyed repute in the age, inherited the enfeoffment as Prince of Huaiyang, and was repeatedly promoted to Inspector of Cang Province.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Xiaoyou won early renown, inherited the title Prince of Huaiyang, and rose through repeated appointments to Inspector of Cang Province.

sentences.zh: 為政溫和，好行小惠，不能清白，而無所侵犯，百姓亦以此便之。

translations.literal: In government he was mild and gentle, fond of granting small favors; he could not keep himself pure, yet he encroached on no one, and the common people likewise found this convenient.
translations.idiomatic: He governed mildly and generously with small favors; though he could not keep his hands clean, he did not prey on the people, who found his rule easy to live under.

sentences.zh: 孝靜帝宴齊文襄王於華林園，孝友因醉自譽，又云陛下許賜臣能。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaojing feasted Prince Wenxiang of Qi in the Hualin Park; Xiaoyou, being drunk, praised himself, and also said, "Your Majesty promised to grant your servant ability."
translations.idiomatic: At a feast for Prince Wenxiang of Qi in the Hualin Park, Emperor Xiaojing heard the drunken Xiaoyou praise himself and claim that the throne had promised him talent.

sentences.zh: 帝笑曰：「朕恒聞王自道清。

translations.literal: The emperor laughed and said, "I constantly hear the Prince call himself pure."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and said, "I am always hearing you call yourself incorruptible."

sentences.zh: 」文襄曰：「臨淮王雅旨舍罪。

translations.literal: " Wenxiang said, "The Prince of Linhuai graciously intends to pardon the offense."
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang added, "The Prince of Linhuai graciously means to let the matter pass."

sentences.zh: 」於是君臣俱笑而不罪。

translations.literal: " Thereupon ruler and ministers all laughed and did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Ruler and ministers all laughed, and no one punished him.

sentences.zh: 孝友明於政理，嘗奏表曰：

translations.literal: Xiaoyou was clear in governmental principle and once submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Clear in affairs of government, Xiaoyou once submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 令制：百家為黨族，二十家為閭，五家為比隣。

translations.literal: The present regulations: a hundred households form a clan-group, twenty households a lane, and five households a close neighborhood.
translations.idiomatic: Under current regulations, a hundred households form a clan-group, twenty a lane, and five a close neighborhood.

sentences.zh: 百家之內，有帥二十五，[10]徵發皆免，苦樂不均。

translations.literal: Within a hundred households there are twenty-five leaders;[10] all are exempt from levies and corvée, so hardship and ease are not equal.
translations.idiomatic: Within each group of a hundred households there are twenty-five leaders,[10] all exempt from levies and corvée, so burdens fall unequally.

sentences.zh: 羊少狼多，復有蠶食。

translations.literal: Few are the sheep and many the wolves; moreover there is nibbling away.
translations.idiomatic: Too few bear the load and too many feed on it, with constant encroachment besides.

sentences.zh: 此之為弊久矣。

translations.literal: The harm in this has long endured.
translations.idiomatic: This abuse has gone on for a very long time.

sentences.zh: 京邑諸坊，或七八百家，唯一里正、二史，庶事無闕，而況外州乎？

translations.literal: In the wards of the capital some have seven or eight hundred households, with only one lane chief and two clerks, yet nothing is wanting in common affairs — how much more in the outer provinces?
translations.idiomatic: In the capital wards some hold seven or eight hundred households with only one lane chief and two clerks, yet routine affairs are not neglected — how much more so in the provinces?

sentences.zh: 請依舊置，三正之名不改，而百家為四閭，閭二比。

translations.literal: I ask that the old arrangement be restored: the names of the three chiefs remain unchanged, while a hundred households form four lanes, and each lane two neighborhoods.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that we restore the old arrangement, keep the titles of the three chiefs unchanged, make a hundred households into four lanes, and each lane into two neighborhoods.

sentences.zh: 計族省十二丁，得十二匹貲絹。

translations.literal: By the reckoning, a clan-group would save twelve adult males and yield twelve bolts of levy silk.
translations.idiomatic: By this reckoning each clan-group would spare twelve adult males and yield twelve bolts of levy silk.

sentences.zh: 略計見管之戶，應二萬餘族，一歲出貲絹二十四萬匹。

translations.literal: A rough estimate of households presently administered comes to more than twenty thousand clan-groups; in one year that would produce two hundred forty thousand bolts of levy silk.
translations.idiomatic: Roughly estimating the households now under administration at more than twenty thousand clan-groups, one year would yield two hundred forty thousand bolts of levy silk.

sentences.zh: 十五丁出一番兵，計得一萬六千兵。

translations.literal: One rotation of troops for every fifteen adult males would yield sixteen thousand soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Requiring one soldier for every fifteen adult males would yield sixteen thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 此富國安人之道也。

translations.literal: This is the way to enrich the state and settle the people.
translations.idiomatic: This is the way to enrich the state and bring peace to the people.

sentences.zh: 古諸侯娶九女，士有一妻、二妾。

translations.literal: In antiquity feudal lords took nine wives; gentlemen had one wife and two concubines.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity feudal lords took nine wives, and gentlemen kept one wife and two concubines.

sentences.zh: 晉令：諸王置妾八人，郡公、侯妾六人。

translations.literal: The Jin code: princes might set up eight concubines; commandery dukes and marquises, six.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Jin code, princes could take eight concubines and commandery dukes and marquises six.

sentences.zh: 官品令：第一、第二品有四妾，第三、第四有三妾，第五、第六有二妾，第七、第八有一妾。

translations.literal: The office-rank code: the first and second ranks had four concubines; the third and fourth, three; the fifth and sixth, two; the seventh and eighth, one.
translations.idiomatic: The office-rank code allowed four concubines for the first and second ranks, three for the third and fourth, two for the fifth and sixth, and one for the seventh and eighth.

sentences.zh: 所以陰教聿修，繼嗣有廣。

translations.literal: Thus the instruction of the inner quarters was greatly cultivated, and continuation of the line was broadened.
translations.idiomatic: Thus women's instruction within the household was cultivated and the line of succession was broadened.

sentences.zh: 廣繼嗣，孝也；

translations.literal: To broaden succession is filial piety;
translations.idiomatic: To broaden the succession is filial;

sentences.zh: 修陰教，禮也。

translations.literal: to cultivate the instruction of the inner quarters is ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: to cultivate the inner quarters is ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 而聖朝忽棄此數，由來漸久。

translations.literal: Yet the sage court has suddenly cast aside these numbers, and the neglect has grown gradual and long.
translations.idiomatic: Yet our court has abruptly abandoned these quotas, and the custom has deepened over time.

sentences.zh: 將相多尚公主，王侯亦娶后族，故無妾媵，習以為常。

translations.literal: Ministers and generals mostly married imperial princesses; kings and marquises also took empresses' kin — hence no concubines and secondary wives, and the practice became the norm.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers and generals mostly married imperial princesses, and kings and marquises took empresses' kin as wives, so they kept no concubines and the habit became normal.

sentences.zh: 婦人多幸，生逢今世，舉朝略是無妾，天下殆皆一妻。

translations.literal: Women are greatly fortunate, born in this age: the whole court is almost without concubines, and under Heaven nearly all have but one wife.
translations.idiomatic: Women are fortunate indeed to live in this age: the whole court scarcely keeps concubines, and the realm is nearly all monogamous.

sentences.zh: 設令人強志廣娶，則家道離索，身事迍邅，內外親知，共相嗤怪。

translations.literal: Suppose one forced his will and took many wives: his household would be scattered, his affairs would go awry, and kin inside and out would together mock him.
translations.idiomatic: Suppose a man forced his will and took many wives: his household would fall apart, his affairs would go awry, and relatives near and far would mock him.

sentences.zh: 凡今之人，通無準節。

translations.literal: As for people today, universally there is no fixed standard.
translations.idiomatic: People today universally lack a fixed standard.

sentences.zh: 父母嫁女，則教之以妒；

translations.literal: When parents marry off a daughter, they teach her jealousy;
translations.idiomatic: When parents marry off a daughter, they teach her to be jealous;

sentences.zh: 姑姊逢迎，必相勸以忌。

translations.literal: when aunts and elder sisters greet her, they are sure to urge her to be forbidding.
translations.idiomatic: when aunts and elder sisters receive her, they urge her to be forbidding.

sentences.zh: 持制夫為婦德，以能妬為女工。

translations.literal: To control the husband is deemed a wife's virtue; to be able to be jealous is deemed a woman's craft.
translations.idiomatic: Controlling the husband is called wifely virtue, and skill in jealousy is called woman's craft.

sentences.zh: 自云不受人欺，[11]畏他笑我。

translations.literal: They say themselves that they will not be bullied by others,[11] yet fear that others will laugh at them.
translations.idiomatic: They say they will not be imposed upon,[11] yet fear being laughed at.

sentences.zh: 王公猶自一心，已下何敢二意。

translations.literal: Even kings and dukes keep but one heart — how dare those below harbor two?
translations.idiomatic: Even kings and dukes keep to one heart; how dare those below harbor two?

sentences.zh: 夫妬忌之心生，則妻妾之禮廢；

translations.literal: When the heart of jealousy arises, the rites of wife and concubine are abandoned;
translations.idiomatic: When jealousy arises, the rites governing wife and concubine are abandoned;

sentences.zh: 妻妾之禮廢，則姦淫之兆興。

translations.literal: when the rites of wife and concubine are abandoned, the omens of licentiousness arise.
translations.idiomatic: when those rites are abandoned, the omens of licentiousness appear.

sentences.zh: 斯臣之所以毒恨者也。

translations.literal: This is what your servant bitterly hates.
translations.idiomatic: This is what your servant bitterly deplores.

sentences.zh: 請以王公第一品娶八，通妻以備九女；

translations.literal: I ask that princes and dukes of the first rank take eight wives, the principal wife counting toward the full nine;
translations.idiomatic: I ask that princes and dukes of the first rank take eight wives, with the principal wife counting toward the full nine;

sentences.zh: 稱事二品備七；

translations.literal: those of the second rank, seven according to office;
translations.idiomatic: those of the second rank, seven according to office;

sentences.zh: 三品、四品備五；

translations.literal: the third and fourth ranks, five;
translations.idiomatic: the third and fourth ranks, five;

sentences.zh: 五品、六品則一妻、二妾。

translations.literal: the fifth and sixth ranks, one wife and two concubines.
translations.idiomatic: the fifth and sixth ranks, one wife and two concubines.

sentences.zh: 限以一周，悉令充數，若不充數及待妾非禮，使妻妒加捶撻，免所居官。

translations.literal: Set a limit of one cycle: all must fill the quota; if they do not fill the quota, or keep concubines contrary to ritual, or let the wife's jealousy add beatings, remove them from office held.
translations.idiomatic: Within one year all must meet the quota; if they fail to meet it, keep concubines contrary to ritual, or let a jealous wife beat them, strip them of office.

sentences.zh: 其妻無子而不娶妾，斯則自絕，無以血食祖父，請科不孝之罪，離遣其妻。

translations.literal: If the wife has no son and he does not take a concubine, that is self-extinction — he cannot offer blood sacrifice to his ancestors; I ask that the crime of unfilial conduct be applied and his wife divorced and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: If a wife bears no son and he will not take a concubine, he cuts off his own line and cannot feed his ancestors by sacrifice; apply the crime of unfilial conduct and divorce the wife.

sentences.zh: 臣之赤心，義唯家國，欲使吉凶無不合禮，貴賤各有其宜，省人帥以出兵丁，立倉儲以豐穀食，設賞格以擒姦盜，行典令以示朝章，庶使足食足兵，人信之矣。

translations.literal: Your servant's loyal heart, in righteousness, is only for family and state: I wish fortune and misfortune all to accord with ritual, noble and base each to have its place; to reduce leaders and thereby raise soldier levies, to establish granaries and thereby enrich grain, to set reward regulations and thereby capture thieves, to enact canonical statutes and thereby display the court's laws — then perhaps food and arms will suffice, and the people will trust.
translations.idiomatic: My loyal heart is for family and state alone: I wish fortune and misfortune to accord with ritual and noble and base each to have its place; to cut neighborhood chiefs and raise levies of soldiers, to build granaries and fill them with grain, to set bounties for catching thieves, and to publish statutes so that arms and food suffice and the people trust the throne.

sentences.zh: 又冒申妻妾之數，正欲使王侯、將相、功臣子弟，苗胤滿朝，傳祚無窮，此臣之志也。

translations.literal: I also venture to state the number of wives and concubines, intending only that the sons and grandsons of kings, dukes, ministers, generals, and meritorious servants fill the court with descendants and transmit blessing without end — this is your servant's aim.
translations.idiomatic: I also venture to prescribe numbers of wives and concubines so that the sons and grandsons of the royal and ministerial houses may fill the court with heirs and transmit blessing without end — that is my aim.

sentences.zh: 詔付有司議奏不同。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the relevant offices to deliberate and memorialize; they differed and did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: The throne referred the matter to the relevant offices for deliberation; their opinions differed and the proposal was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 孝友又言：「今人生為皁隸，葬擬王侯，存沒異途，無復節制，崇壯丘壠，盛飾祭儀，隣里相榮，稱為至孝。

translations.literal: Xiaoyou also said: "Today men are born black-collared bondsmen, yet in burial they rival kings and marquises; alive and dead take different roads, with no restraint left; they mound lofty tombs and lavish funeral rites, and neighbors hold one another glorious, calling it utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyou also said: "Today men live as commoners yet bury themselves like kings and marquises; in life and death alike restraint is gone; they heap lofty tombs and lavish funeral rites, and neighbors praise one another, calling it utmost filial piety.

sentences.zh: 又夫婦之始，王化所先，共食合瓢，足以成禮。

translations.literal: Moreover the beginning of husband and wife is what royal transformation takes first; sharing food and joining gourds is enough to complete the rite.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the bond of husband and wife is where royal transformation begins; sharing food and joining halves of a gourd is enough to complete the rite.

sentences.zh: 而今之富者彌奢，同牢之設，甚於祭槃。

translations.literal: Yet the rich today grow ever more extravagant; the setting out of the shared wedding meal exceeds the sacrificial trays.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the rich grow ever more extravagant; their wedding feasts outdo sacrificial banquets.

sentences.zh: 累魚成山，山有林木，林木之上，鸞鳳斯存。

translations.literal: They pile fish into mountains, and on the mountains place trees; above the trees perch phoenixes.
translations.idiomatic: They pile fish into mountains, set trees upon the mountains, and place phoenixes in the trees.

sentences.zh: 徒有煩勞，終成委棄，仰惟天意，其或不然。

translations.literal: It is only vain labor, ending in abandonment; looking up to Heaven's intent, surely it cannot be so.
translations.idiomatic: All of it is vain labor doomed to be cast away; Heaven's intent, surely, cannot approve.

sentences.zh: 請自茲以後，若婚葬過禮者，[12]以違旨論，官司不加糾劾，即與同罪。」

translations.literal: I ask that from this time forward, if wedding or funeral exceeds ritual,[12] it be judged as defying the imperial will; if officials do not investigate and impeach, they share the crime."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that hereafter anyone whose wedding or funeral exceeds ritual[12] be punished as defying the throne, and that officials who fail to investigate share the guilt."

sentences.zh: 孝友在尹積年，[13]以法自守，甚著聲稱。

translations.literal: Xiaoyou served as Intendant of the Capital for many years,[13] keeping himself by the law and winning great repute.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyou served many years as Intendant of the Capital,[13] held himself to the law, and won a strong reputation.

sentences.zh: 然性無骨鯁，善事權勢，為正直者所譏。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he lacked unbending fiber, was good at courting the powerful, and men of upright character ridiculed him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he lacked backbone by nature, courted the powerful, and upright men ridiculed him.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，爵例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, noble ranks were reduced according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, noble ranks were lowered according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 昌弟孚，字秀和。

translations.literal: Chang's younger brother Fu, styled Xiuhe.
translations.idiomatic: Fu, younger brother of Chang, styled Xiuhe.

sentences.zh: 少有令譽，侍中游肇、并州刺史高聰、司徒崔光等見孚，咸曰：「此子當準的人物，恨吾徒衰暮，不及見耳。

translations.literal: From youth he had fine repute; when Attendant-in-Chief You Zhao, Inspector of Bing Province Gao Cong, Minister of State Cui Guang, and others saw Fu, they all said, "This boy will measure up to a man of mark; we regret that our company is aged and declining and will not live to see it."
translations.idiomatic: From youth he enjoyed fine repute. When Attendant-in-Chief You Zhao, Inspector of Bing Province Gao Cong, Minister of State Cui Guang, and others met Fu, they all said, "This boy will become a man of mark; we regret our old age and will not live to see it."

sentences.zh: 」累遷兼尚書右丞。

translations.literal: " He was repeatedly promoted to Acting Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Acting Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 靈太后臨朝，宦者干政，孚乃總括古今名妃賢后，凡為四卷，奏之。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling held court, eunuchs meddled in government; Fu thereupon compiled famous consorts and worthy empresses of antiquity and the present into four scrolls and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling held court and eunuchs meddled in affairs, Fu compiled famous consorts and worthy empresses through the ages in four scrolls and submitted them.

sentences.zh: 遷左丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕王阿那瓌既得返國，其人大飢，相率入塞，阿那瓌上表請臺賑給。

translations.literal: After the Rouran king Anagui had been restored to his state, his people suffered great famine and entered the passes in a body; Anagui submitted a memorial requesting court relief.
translations.idiomatic: After the Rouran king Anagui returned to his realm, his people starved and poured through the passes; Anagui memorialized the court for relief.

sentences.zh: 詔孚為北道行臺，詣彼賑恤。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Fu Northern Route Commissioner to go there and give relief.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Fu Northern Route Commissioner to go and relieve them.

sentences.zh: 孚陳便宜，表曰：

translations.literal: Fu set forth what was expedient and submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Fu proposed what was expedient in a memorial:

sentences.zh: 皮服之人，未嘗粒食。

translations.literal: People who wear hides have never eaten grain.
translations.idiomatic: People who dress in hides have never lived on grain.

sentences.zh: 宜從俗因利，拯其所無。

translations.literal: One should follow custom and profit by circumstance, and rescue them in what they lack.
translations.idiomatic: One should follow their customs and circumstances and supply what they lack.

sentences.zh: 昔漢建武中，單于款塞，時轉河東米糒二萬五千斛、牛羊三萬六千頭以給之。

translations.literal: In the Jianwu era of Han, when the Chanyu submitted at the passes, they then transported twenty-five thousand hu of rice gruel from Hedong and thirty-six thousand head of cattle and sheep to supply him.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jianwu era of Han, when the Chanyu submitted at the passes, the court sent twenty-five thousand hu of rice from Hedong and thirty-six thousand head of cattle and sheep.

sentences.zh: 斯即前代和戎、撫新、柔遠之長策也。

translations.literal: That was the long policy of former ages: harmonizing with the barbarians, comforting the new, and gentling the distant.
translations.idiomatic: That was the long-tested policy of former ages for harmonizing with barbarians, comforting newcomers, and gentling the distant.

sentences.zh: 乞以牸牛產羊餬其口命。

translations.literal: I beg that cows and breeding sheep be granted to feed their mouths and lives.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that cows and breeding sheep be granted to sustain their lives.

sentences.zh: 且畜牧繁息，是其所便，毛血之利，惠兼衣食。

translations.literal: Moreover livestock multiply easily — that is what suits them; the profit of hide and blood benefits both clothing and food.
translations.idiomatic: Livestock moreover breed readily, which suits them; hides and blood profit both clothing and food.

sentences.zh: 又尚書奏云，如其仍住七州，隨寬置之。

translations.literal: The Secretariat also memorialized that if they remain in the seven provinces, they should be settled wherever space allows.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat also memorialized that if they remain in the seven provinces, they should be settled wherever there is room.

sentences.zh: 臣謂人情戀本，寧肯徙內。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that men's feelings cling to their native place; they would rather not move inward.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that people cling to their native soil and would rather not move inland.

sentences.zh: 若依臣請，給賑雜畜，愛本重鄉，必還舊土。

translations.literal: If my request is followed and mixed livestock is given in relief, cherishing the root and honoring the village, they will surely return to their old lands.
translations.idiomatic: If my request is granted and mixed herds are given in relief, loving their roots and honoring their homes, they will surely return to their old lands.

sentences.zh: 如其不然，禁留益損。

translations.literal: If it is not so, detaining them will only increase the harm.
translations.idiomatic: If not, detaining them will only increase the harm.

sentences.zh: 假令逼徙，事非久計。

translations.literal: Even if they are forced to move, the measure will not last.
translations.idiomatic: Even forced relocation cannot be a lasting policy.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 人面獸心，去留難測，既易水草，痾恙將多，憂愁致困，死亡必甚。

translations.literal: Human in face but beast in heart — whether they stay or go is hard to gauge; once fodder and water change, sickness will multiply; worry and distress will bring exhaustion, and death will surely be severe.
translations.idiomatic: Their faces are human but their hearts bestial; stay or go is hard to predict; change their fodder and water and sickness will multiply; grief and hardship will wear them down and deaths will be many.

sentences.zh: 兼其餘類尚在沙磧，脫出狂勃，翻歸舊巢，必殘掠邑里，遺毒百姓。

translations.literal: Moreover the rest of their kind remain in the sandy wastes; if they break out in violent rage and turn back to their old nests, they will surely ravage the districts and leave poison among the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover their kinsmen remain in the deserts; if they burst into violence and return to their old haunts, they will ravage the districts and harm the people.

sentences.zh: 亂而方塞，未若杜其未萌。

translations.literal: To try to block the disorder once it has begun is not as good as stopping it before it sprouts.
translations.idiomatic: Blocking disorder after it has begun is inferior to stopping it before it sprouts.

sentences.zh: 又貿遷起於上古，交易行於中世，漢與胡通，亦立關巿。

translations.literal: Trade too arose in high antiquity; exchange flourished in the middle ages; Han too, in dealing with the Hu, established border markets.
translations.idiomatic: Commerce arose in high antiquity and exchange in the middle ages; Han too established border markets in dealing with the Hu.

sentences.zh: 今北人阻飢，命懸溝壑，公給之外，必求巿易，彼若願求，宜見聽許。

translations.literal: Now the northerners are cut off by famine, their lives hanging over gullies and ravines; beyond public grants they are sure to seek market trade — if they wish to buy, it should be permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The northerners are starving, their lives over the abyss; beyond public relief they will surely seek to trade, and if they wish to buy, they should be allowed.

sentences.zh: 又云：

translations.literal: He also said:
translations.idiomatic: He also said:

sentences.zh: 營大者不計小名，圖遠者弗拘近利。

translations.literal: One who plans on a great scale does not count small names; one who plots far does not bind himself to near profit.
translations.idiomatic: Great undertakings do not fuss over small reputations; far-sighted plans do not cling to immediate gain.

sentences.zh: 雖戎狄衰盛，歷代不同，叛服之情，略可論討。

translations.literal: Though the Rong and Di weaken and strengthen through the ages in different ways, the bent of submission and rebellion can broadly be discussed and weighed.
translations.idiomatic: Though the barbarians' strength shifts from age to age, the pattern of submission and rebellion can broadly be judged.

sentences.zh: 周之北伐，僅獲中規；

translations.literal: When Zhou campaigned north, it barely won a middling success;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's northern campaigns won only middling success;

sentences.zh: 漢氏外攘，裁收下策。

translations.literal: when Han pressed outward, it barely achieved the lower strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Han outward expansion barely achieved the lesser strategy.

sentences.zh: 昔在代京，恒為重備，將帥勞止，甲士疲力。

translations.literal: Formerly at the capital in Dai it was always heavily garrisoned; generals and commanders grew weary and halted, soldiers and armor were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly at Dai the capital was always heavily garrisoned; commanders wore themselves out and armored men were exhausted.

sentences.zh: 前世苦之，計未能致。

translations.literal: Former ages suffered from it; by plan they could not reach a solution.
translations.idiomatic: Former ages suffered from this and could not solve it by planning.

sentences.zh: 今天祚大魏，亂亡在彼。

translations.literal: Today Heaven's mandate rests on Great Wei, and disorder and ruin lie with them.
translations.idiomatic: Today Heaven's mandate rests on Great Wei, while disorder and ruin lie with them.

sentences.zh: 朝廷垂天覆之恩，廓大造之德。

translations.literal: The court extends the grace that covers heaven and the virtue of vast creation.
translations.idiomatic: The court extends grace that covers heaven and the virtue of vast creation.

sentences.zh: 鳩其散亡，禮送令返。

translations.literal: It gathers their scattered people, treats them with ritual, and sends them back under command.
translations.idiomatic: It gathers their scattered people, treats them with ritual, and sends them home under command.

sentences.zh: 宜因此時，善思遠策。

translations.literal: One should at this time think well on a far-reaching policy.
translations.idiomatic: This is the time to devise a far-reaching policy.

sentences.zh: 竊以理雖萬變，可以一觀；

translations.literal: Your servant holds that though principle has ten thousand changes, it may be viewed from one standpoint;
translations.idiomatic: Though principle has ten thousand changes, it may be viewed from one standpoint;

sentences.zh: 來事雖懸，易以往卜。

translations.literal: though coming events hang in suspense, the past may be used to divine them.
translations.idiomatic: though the future is uncertain, the past may be used to divine it.

sentences.zh: 昔漢宣之世，呼韓款塞，漢遣董忠、韓昌領邊郡士馬，送出朔方，因留衞助。

translations.literal: In the era of Han Xuandi, Huhanye submitted at the passes; Han sent Dong Zhong and Han Chang to lead border commandery troops and horses, escort him out through Shuofang, and there remain to guard and assist.
translations.idiomatic: In the era of Han Xuandi, Huhanye submitted at the passes; Han sent Dong Zhong and Han Chang with border troops and horses to escort him out through Shuofang and remain to guard and assist.

sentences.zh: 又光武時，亦令中郎將段彬置安集掾史，隨單于所在，參察動靜。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Guangwu as well, the court ordered Palace Attendant Duan Bin to appoint pacification clerks who would follow the Chanyu wherever he went and observe movements.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Guangwu as well, the court ordered Palace Attendant Duan Bin to appoint pacification clerks to follow the Chanyu and observe his movements.

sentences.zh: 斯皆守吉之元龜，安邊之勝策。

translations.literal: These are the great tortoises of guarding antiquity, the winning policies for securing the border.
translations.idiomatic: These are the great tortoises of guarding antiquity, the winning policies for securing the frontier.

sentences.zh: 計今朝廷成功，不減曩時；

translations.literal: Considering the present, the court's accomplishment is no less than in those times;
translations.idiomatic: The court's accomplishment today is no less than in those times;

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕國弊，亦同疇日。

translations.literal: the Rouran state's exhaustion is likewise as in those days.
translations.idiomatic: the Rouran state's exhaustion is likewise the same.

sentences.zh: 宜準昔成謨，略依舊事。

translations.literal: One should take former successful plans as the standard and broadly follow the old precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Take former successful plans as the standard and broadly follow old precedents.

sentences.zh: 借其所閑地，聽使田牧；

translations.literal: Lend them idle land and allow them to farm and pasture;
translations.idiomatic: Lend them idle land and let them farm and pasture;

sentences.zh: 粗置官屬，示相慰撫；

translations.literal: Set up officials in rough outline and show mutual comfort and consolation;
translations.idiomatic: Post a modest staff to offer reassurance and comfort;

sentences.zh: 嚴戒邊兵，以見保衞。

translations.literal: Strictly warn the border troops, thereby making protection visible;
translations.idiomatic: Strictly warn the border troops to show that protection is at hand;

sentences.zh: 馭以寬仁，縻以久策。

translations.literal: Guide them with breadth and kindness, tether them with a long-term policy;
translations.idiomatic: Govern them with magnanimity and bind them with a long-range policy;

sentences.zh: 使親不至矯詐，疏不容叛反。

translations.literal: Let the close not reach to feigned deceit, nor the distant harbor rebellion;
translations.idiomatic: Keep intimates from deception and the distant from rebellion;

sentences.zh: 今北鎮諸將舊常云一人代外邏，[14]因令防察。

translations.literal: Now the generals of the northern garrisons have long customarily said that one man deputizes for outer patrol,[14] and thus are ordered to inspect and guard;
translations.idiomatic: The northern garrison commanders have long had one man deputize for outer patrol,[14] and use that arrangement for surveillance;

sentences.zh: 所謂天子有道，守在四夷者也。

translations.literal: This is what is called: when the Son of Heaven has the Way, defense lies with the four barbarians;
translations.idiomatic: That is what is meant by saying that when the Son of Heaven holds the Way, defense rests with the four quarters;

sentences.zh: 又云：

translations.literal: He also said:
translations.idiomatic: He also said:

sentences.zh: 先人有奪人之心，待降如受強敵。

translations.literal: The former men had hearts that seized on others; they treated submission like receiving a strong foe;
translations.idiomatic: Our forebears treated submitters like powerful enemies, bent on seizing advantage;

sentences.zh: 武非專外，亦以防內。

translations.literal: Arms are not solely for without; they also defend within;
translations.idiomatic: Arms serve not only the frontier but also internal security;

sentences.zh: 若從處分割配，諸州鎮遼遠，非轉輸可到，悔叛之情，變起難測。

translations.literal: If they are allocated by division from their stations, the provinces and garrisons are remote in distance and reach, not places transfer and transport can reach; feelings of regret and rebellion will arise, and changes will be hard to foresee;
translations.idiomatic: If they are split up and reassigned, the provinces and garrisons are too distant for supply lines; regret and defection will arise and changes will be unpredictable;

sentences.zh: 又居人畜業，布在原野，戎夷性貪，見則思盜。

translations.literal: Moreover they dwell with their livestock and herds spread on the open steppe; the Rong and Di are greedy by nature — seeing them, they think to steal;
translations.idiomatic: Their herds roam the open steppe, and the barbarians are greedy by nature — where they see livestock they think of theft;

sentences.zh: 防彼肅此，少兵不堪，渾流之際，易相干犯。

translations.literal: To guard there and secure here, few troops will not suffice; when flows mingle, offenses against one another come easily;
translations.idiomatic: Guarding them while securing our own side takes more troops than we have; when the populations mingle, clashes come easily;

sentences.zh: 驅之還本，未必樂去，配州內徙，復不肯從。

translations.literal: Driving them back to their roots, they will not necessarily be glad to leave; assigning them to provinces for inward relocation, again they will not consent;
translations.idiomatic: Drive them home and they may not wish to go; assign them to inland provinces and again they will refuse;

sentences.zh: 既其如此，為費必大。

translations.literal: Since matters stand thus, the cost will surely be great.
translations.idiomatic: Since matters stand thus, the cost will surely be great.

sentences.zh: 朝廷不許。

translations.literal: The court did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not permit it.

sentences.zh: 孚持白虎幡勞阿那瓌於柔玄、懷荒二鎮間。

translations.literal: Fu, bearing the white-tiger banner, went to comfort Anagui between the Rouxuan and Huaihuang garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Fu, bearing the white-tiger banner, went to comfort Anagui between the Rouxuan and Huaihuang garrisons.

sentences.zh: 阿那瓌眾號三十萬，陰有異意，遂拘留孚，載以轀車，日給酪一升，肉一段。

translations.literal: Anagui's followers were said to number three hundred thousand; harboring secret designs, he detained Fu, carried him in a covered wagon, and each day gave him one sheng of kumiss and one portion of meat.
translations.idiomatic: Anagui's followers were said to number three hundred thousand; harboring secret designs, he detained Fu, carried him in a covered wagon, and each day gave him one sheng of kumiss and one portion of meat.

sentences.zh: 每集其眾，坐孚東廂，稱為行臺，甚加禮敬。

translations.literal: Whenever he assembled his host, he seated Fu in the eastern wing, called him Commissioner, and showed him great respect.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he assembled his host, he seated Fu in the eastern wing, called him Commissioner, and showed him great respect.

sentences.zh: 阿那瓌遂南過至舊京，後遣孚等還，因上表謝罪。

translations.literal: Anagui then passed south as far as the old capital; afterward he sent Fu and the others back and submitted a memorial asking pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Anagui then passed south as far as the old capital; afterward he sent Fu and the others back and submitted a memorial asking pardon.

sentences.zh: 有司以孚事下廷尉，丞高謙之云孚辱命，處孚流罪。

translations.literal: The relevant offices referred Fu's case to the Court of Justice; Vice Director Gao Qianzhi said Fu had disgraced his commission and sentenced him to exile.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices referred Fu's case to the Court of Justice; Vice Director Gao Qianzhi said Fu had disgraced his commission and sentenced him to exile.

sentences.zh: 後拜冀州刺史，孚勸課農桑，境內稱為慈父，隣州號曰神君。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Inspector of Ji Province; Fu urged farming and sericulture, and within the province he was called a kindly father, while neighboring provinces called him a divine lord.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Inspector of Ji Province; Fu urged farming and sericulture, and within the province he was called a kindly father, while neighboring provinces called him a divine lord.

sentences.zh: 先是，州人張孟都、張洪建、馬潘、崔獨憐、張叔緒、崔醜、張天宜、崔思哲等八家，皆屯保林野，不臣王命，州郡號曰八王。

translations.literal: Before this, eight clans of the province — Zhang Mengdu, Zhang Hongjian, Ma Pan, Cui Dulian, Zhang Shuxu, Cui Chou, Zhang Tianyi, and Cui Sizhe — all held fortified camps in forest and wild and did not submit to the royal command; the province and commanderies called them the Eight Kings.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, eight clans of the province — Zhang Mengdu, Zhang Hongjian, Ma Pan, Cui Dulian, Zhang Shuxu, Cui Chou, Zhang Tianyi, and Cui Sizhe — all held fortified camps in forest and wild and did not submit to the royal command; the province and commanderies called them the Eight Kings.

sentences.zh: 孚至，皆請入城，願致死効力。

translations.literal: When Fu arrived, all asked to enter the cities and pledged to die in his service.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu arrived, all asked to enter the cities and pledged to die in his service.

sentences.zh: 後為葛榮所陷，為榮所執。

translations.literal: Later he was overrun by Ge Rong and seized by him.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was overrun by Ge Rong and seized by him.

sentences.zh: 兄祐為防城都督，兄子子禮為錄事參軍，榮欲先害子禮，孚請先死以贖子禮，叩頭流血，榮乃捨之。

translations.literal: His elder brother You was Defense Commander of the city; his brother's son Zili was Recording Secretary; Ge Rong wished first to kill Zili, but Fu begged to die first in Zili's stead, knocking his head until it bled, and Ge Rong thereupon spared him.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother You was Defense Commander of the city; his brother's son Zili was Recording Secretary; Ge Rong wished first to kill Zili, but Fu begged to die first in Zili's stead, knocking his head until it bled, and Ge Rong thereupon spared him.

sentences.zh: 又大集將士議其死事，孚兄弟各誣己引過，爭相為死。

translations.literal: Ge Rong also gathered officers and men to decide their deaths; Fu and his brothers each falsely accused themselves and vied to die in the other's place.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Rong also gathered officers and men to decide their deaths; Fu and his brothers each falsely accused themselves and vied to die in the other's place.

sentences.zh: 又孟都、潘、紹等數百人皆叩頭就法，[15]請活使君。

translations.literal: Moreover Mengdu, Pan, Shao, and several hundred others all knocked their heads and submitted to the law,[15] begging that the commissioner be spared.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Mengdu, Pan, Shao, and several hundred others all knocked their heads and submitted to the law,[15] begging that the commissioner be spared.

sentences.zh: 榮曰：「此魏之誠臣義士也。

translations.literal: Ge Rong said: "These are Wei's loyal servants and men of righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Rong said: "These are Wei's loyal servants and men of righteousness.

sentences.zh: 」凡同禁五百人，皆得免。

translations.literal: " In all, five hundred men held together in detention were spared.
translations.idiomatic: In all, five hundred men held together in detention were spared.

sentences.zh: 榮平，[16]還，除冀州刺史。

translations.literal: When Ge Rong was pacified,[16] Fu returned and was again made Inspector of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: When Ge Rong was pacified,[16] Fu returned and was again made Inspector of Ji.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，授孚東道行臺、彭城郡王，孚封顥逆書送朝廷，天子嘉之。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Fu was made Eastern Route Commissioner and Prince of Pengcheng; Fu sealed Yuan Hao's treasonous letter and sent it to court, and the Son of Heaven praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Fu was made Eastern Route Commissioner and Prince of Pengcheng; Fu sealed Yuan Hao's treasonous letter and sent it to court, and the Son of Heaven praised him.

sentences.zh: 顥平，封孚萬年鄉男。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao was defeated, Fu was enfeoffed as Baron of Wannian Township.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao was defeated, Fu was enfeoffed as Baron of Wannian Township.

sentences.zh: 永安末，樂器殘缺，莊帝命孚監儀注，孚上表曰：「昔太和中，中書監高閭、太樂令公孫崇修造金石，數十年間，乃奏成功。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yongan era, musical instruments were damaged and incomplete; Emperor Zhuang ordered Fu to supervise ritual regulations. Fu submitted a memorial: "In the Taihe era, Director of the Secretariat Gao Lao and Director of the Grand Music Office Gongsun Chong repaired and cast metal and stone instruments; only after several decades was success reported.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yongan era, musical instruments were damaged and incomplete; Emperor Zhuang ordered Fu to supervise ritual regulations. Fu submitted a memorial: "In the Taihe era, Director of the Secretariat Gao Lao and Director of the Grand Music Office Gongsun Chong repaired and cast metal and stone instruments; only after several decades was success reported.

sentences.zh: 時大集儒生，考其得失。

translations.literal: At that time the court greatly gathered Confucian scholars to examine what was right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court greatly gathered Confucian scholars to examine what was right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 太常卿劉芳請別營造，久而方就。

translations.literal: Minister of Ceremonies Liu Fang requested a separate construction; only after a long while was it completed.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Ceremonies Liu Fang requested a separate construction; only after a long while was it completed.

sentences.zh: 復召公卿量校合否，論者沸騰，莫有適從。

translations.literal: The court again summoned princes and ministers to weigh whether it was correct; debaters boiled over, and none could agree.
translations.idiomatic: The court again summoned princes and ministers to weigh whether it was correct; debaters boiled over, and none could agree.

sentences.zh: 登被旨敕，並見施用。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen received an imperial directive and all were put into use.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen received an imperial directive and all were put into use.

sentences.zh: 往歲大軍入洛，戎馬交馳，所有樂器，亡失垂盡。

translations.literal: In past years the great army entered Luoyang; war-horses crossed in tumult; nearly all musical instruments were lost.
translations.idiomatic: In past years the great army entered Luoyang; war-horses crossed in tumult; nearly all musical instruments were lost.

sentences.zh: 臣至太樂署，問太樂令張乾龜等，云承前以來，置宮懸四箱，簨簴六架。

translations.literal: Your servant arrived at the Grand Music Office and questioned Grand Music Director Zhang Qiangui and others, who said that from previous times onward they had set up four cases of palace bells and chimes and six bell-frames with feathered shafts.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant arrived at the Grand Music Office and questioned Grand Music Director Zhang Qiangui and others, who said that from previous times onward they had set up four cases of palace bells and chimes and six bell-frames with feathered shafts.

sentences.zh: 東北架編黃鍾之磬十四，雖器名黃鍾，而聲實夷則，考之音制，不甚諧韻。

translations.literal: On the northeast frame were strung fourteen sounding-stones of Huangzhong; though the instrument was named Huangzhong, the tone was actually Yize — examining the pitch system, it was not very harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: On the northeast frame were strung fourteen sounding-stones of Huangzhong; though the instrument was named Huangzhong, the tone was actually Yize — examining the pitch system, it was not very harmonious.

sentences.zh: 姑洗懸於東北，太蔟編於西北，蕤賓列於西南，並皆器象差位，調律不和。

translations.literal: Guxian hung in the northeast, Taicu arrayed in the northwest, Ruibin ranged in the southwest — all had instrument forms and positions at variance, and pitch regulation was not in accord.
translations.idiomatic: Guxian hung in the northeast, Taicu arrayed in the northwest, Ruibin ranged in the southwest — all had instrument forms and positions at variance, and pitch regulation was not in accord.

sentences.zh: 又有儀鍾十四，虛懸架首，初不叩擊，今便刪廢，以從正則。

translations.literal: There were also fourteen ceremonial bells hung vainly at the frame-top and never struck at first; now let them be abolished to follow proper rule.
translations.idiomatic: There were also fourteen ceremonial bells hung vainly at the frame-top and never struck at first; now let them be abolished to follow proper rule.

sentences.zh: 臣今據周禮鳧氏修廣之規，磬氏倨句之法，吹律求聲，叩鍾求音，損除繁雜，討論實錄，依十二月為十二宮，各準辰次，當位懸設，月聲既備，隨用擊奏，則會還相為宮之義，又得律呂相生之體。

translations.literal: Your servant now follows the Regulator's rules of breadth in the Zhou li, the Regulator of Chimes' method of obtuse and acute angles; blowing pipes to seek sound, striking bells to seek pitch; removing the superfluous and discussing what is real — according to the twelve months as twelve palaces, each matching the chronological station, set at the proper position when suspended; once the monthly sounds are complete and struck as needed, then the principle of mutual generation among tones is achieved, and the substance of pitch-pipe mutual generation is obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant now follows the Regulator's rules of breadth in the Zhou li and the Regulator of Chimes' method of obtuse and acute angles; blowing pipes to seek sound and striking bells to seek pitch, I have removed the superfluous and discussed what is real.
