According to the twelve months as twelve palaces, each matching its chronological station, set at the proper position when suspended — once the monthly sounds are complete and struck as needed, the principle of mutual generation among tones is achieved and the substance of pitch-pipe mutual generation is obtained.

sentences.zh: 今量鍾磬之數，各以十二架為定。

translations.literal: Now measuring the number of bells and chimes, set each at twelve frames as fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Now measuring the number of bells and chimes, set each at twelve frames as fixed.

sentences.zh: 」奏可。

translations.literal: " The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 于時搢紳之士，咸往觀聽，靡不咨嗟歎服而返。

translations.literal: At that time gentry and officials all went to observe and listen, and none returned without sighing in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: At that time gentry and officials all went to observe and listen, and none returned without sighing in admiration.

sentences.zh: 太傅、錄尚書長孫承業妙解聲律，特復稱善。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor and Recorder of the Secretariat Changsun Chengye had a marvelous grasp of pitch and mode and especially praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor and Recorder of the Secretariat Changsun Chengye had a marvelous grasp of pitch and mode and especially praised it.

sentences.zh: 後從出帝入關。

translations.literal: Later he followed Emperor Chu exiting the passes westward.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Emperor Chu exiting the passes westward.

sentences.zh: 子石侯，襲。

translations.literal: His son Shihou inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shihou inherited.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡曰哀王。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Prince Ai (Lamented).
translations.idiomatic: He died; posthumous title Prince Ai (Lamented).

sentences.zh: 子遺興，襲。

translations.literal: His son Yixing inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yixing inherited.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡曰定王。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Prince Ding (Settled).
translations.idiomatic: He died; posthumous title Prince Ding (Settled).

sentences.zh: 無子。

translations.literal: He had no son.
translations.idiomatic: He had no son.

sentences.zh: 石侯弟嘉，少沉敏，喜慍不形於色，兼有武略。

translations.literal: Shihou's younger brother Jia, from youth was deep and keen; joy and anger did not show on his face, and he had martial strategy as well.
translations.idiomatic: Shihou's younger brother Jia, from youth was deep and keen; joy and anger did not show on his face, and he had martial strategy as well.

sentences.zh: 高祖初，拜徐州刺史，甚有威惠。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Gaozu's reign he was appointed Inspector of Xu Province and possessed great authority and grace.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Gaozu's reign he was appointed Inspector of Xu Province and possessed great authority and grace.

sentences.zh: 後封廣陽王，以紹建後。

translations.literal: Later he was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangyang to continue the enfeoffment line.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangyang to continue the enfeoffment line.

sentences.zh: 高祖南伐，詔嘉斷均口。

translations.literal: When Gaozu campaigned south, an edict ordered Jia to cut off the Jun ford.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu campaigned south, an edict ordered Jia to cut off the Jun ford.

sentences.zh: 嘉違失指授，令賊得免。

translations.literal: Jia violated and missed the instruction and let the bandits escape.
translations.idiomatic: Jia violated and missed the instruction and let the bandits escape.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，責之曰：「叔祖定非世孫，何太不上類也！

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and rebuked him: "Uncle-forebear Ding was no heir of the age — how can you be so unlike your kind!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and rebuked him: "Uncle-forebear Ding was no heir of the age — how can you be so unlike your kind!

sentences.zh: 」及將大漸，遺詔以嘉為尚書左僕射，與咸陽王禧等輔政。

translations.literal: " When he was about to die, his final edict made Jia Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, to assist in government with Prince Xianyang of Xi and others.
translations.idiomatic: When he was about to die, his final edict made Jia Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, to assist in government with Prince Xianyang of Xi and others.

sentences.zh: 遷司州牧，嘉表請於京四面，築坊三百二十，各周一千二百步，乞發三正復丁，以充茲役，雖有暫勞，姦盜永止。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Governor of Si Province; Jia memorialized asking that around the capital on four sides three hundred twenty wards be built, each with a perimeter of twelve hundred paces; he begged that the three chiefs' restored adult males be levied to fill this labor — though there would be temporary toil, brigands and thieves would cease forever.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Governor of Si Province; Jia memorialized asking that around the capital on four sides three hundred twenty wards be built, each with a perimeter of twelve hundred paces; he begged that the three chiefs' restored adult males be levied to fill this labor — though there would be temporary toil, brigands and thieves would cease forever.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict followed his request.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed his request.

sentences.zh: 拜衞大將軍、尚書令，除儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand General of the Guard and Director of the Secretariat, and granted parity of three offices.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Grand General of the Guard and Director of the Secretariat, and granted parity of three offices.

sentences.zh: 嘉好飲酒，或沉醉，在世宗前言笑自得，無所顧忌。

translations.literal: Jia loved wine and sometimes grew drunk; before Emperor Shizong he spoke and laughed as he pleased without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Jia loved wine and sometimes grew drunk; before Emperor Shizong he spoke and laughed as he pleased without restraint.

sentences.zh: 帝以其屬尊年老，常優容之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because of his eminent kinship and advanced age, always treated him leniently.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, because of his eminent kinship and advanced age, always treated him leniently.

sentences.zh: 與彭城、北海、高陽諸王每入宴集，極歡彌夜，數加賞賜。

translations.literal: With the princes of Pengcheng, Beihai, and Gaoyang he entered feast upon feast, reveling through the night, and received frequent rewards.
translations.idiomatic: With the princes of Pengcheng, Beihai, and Gaoyang he entered feast upon feast, reveling through the night, and received frequent rewards.

sentences.zh: 帝亦時幸其第。

translations.literal: The emperor also sometimes visited his mansion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also sometimes visited his mansion.

sentences.zh: 性好儀飾，車服鮮華，既居儀同，又任端首，出入容衞，道路榮之。

translations.literal: By nature he loved ceremony and adornment; carriages and robes were fresh and splendid; having attained parity of three offices and serving as head of the levee, he went out and in with guards and retinue, and the road honored him.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he loved ceremony and adornment; carriages and robes were fresh and splendid; having attained parity of three offices and serving as head of the levee, he went out and in with guards and retinue, and the road honored him.

sentences.zh: 後遷司空，轉司徒。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Minister of Works, then to Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was transferred to Minister of Works, then to Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 嘉好立功名，有益公私，多所敷奏，帝雅委付之。

translations.literal: Jia loved to establish merit and fame; what benefited public and private he often memorialized, and the emperor deeply entrusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Jia loved to establish merit and fame; what benefited public and private he often memorialized, and the emperor deeply entrusted him.

sentences.zh: 愛敬人物，後來才俊未為時知者，侍坐之次，轉加談引，時人以此稱之。

translations.literal: He loved and respected men of talent; when younger men of promise were not yet known to the age, at sessions when seated he would turn and draw them into talk, and men of the time praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: He loved and respected men of talent; when younger men of promise were not yet known to the age, at sessions when seated he would turn and draw them into talk, and men of the time praised him for this.

sentences.zh: 薨，遺命薄葬。

translations.literal: He died and left instructions for a plain burial.
translations.idiomatic: He died and left instructions for a plain burial.

sentences.zh: 世宗悼惜之，贈侍中、太保，諡曰懿烈。

translations.literal: Shizong mourned him and posthumously appointed him Palace Attendant and Grand Tutor, with posthumous title Yi Lie (Steadfast and Ardent).
translations.idiomatic: Shizong mourned him and posthumously appointed him Palace Attendant and Grand Tutor, with posthumous title Yi Lie (Steadfast and Ardent).

sentences.zh: 嘉後妃，宜都王穆壽孫女、司空從妹也，聰明婦人。

translations.literal: Jia's consort was granddaughter of Prince Yidu Mu Shou and younger cousin of the Minister of Works — a clever woman.
translations.idiomatic: Jia's consort was granddaughter of Prince Yidu Mu Shou and younger cousin of the Minister of Works — a clever woman.

sentences.zh: 及為嘉妃，多所匡贊，光益家道。

translations.literal: When she became Jia's princess-consort, she often corrected and assisted him, brightening and enriching the household.
translations.idiomatic: When she became Jia's princess-consort, she often corrected and assisted him, brightening and enriching the household.

sentences.zh: 子深，[18]字智遠，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Shen,[18] styled Zhiyuan, inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shen,[18] styled Zhiyuan, inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 肅宗初，拜肆州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Suzong's reign he was appointed Inspector of Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Suzong's reign he was appointed Inspector of Si Province.

sentences.zh: 預行恩信，胡人便之，劫盜止息。

translations.literal: He beforehand practiced grace and trust; the Hu found him convenient, and robbery and banditry ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He beforehand practiced grace and trust; the Hu found him convenient, and robbery and banditry ceased.

sentences.zh: 後為恒州刺史，在州多所受納，政以賄成，私家有馬千匹者必取百匹，以此為恒。

translations.literal: Later he became Inspector of Heng Province; in the province he received many bribes, and government was accomplished through gifts — households with a thousand horses in private stock he surely took a hundred, and made this the norm.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became Inspector of Heng Province; in the province he received many bribes, and government was accomplished through gifts — households with a thousand horses in private stock he surely took a hundred, and made this the norm.

sentences.zh: 累遷殿中尚書，未拜，坐淫城陽王徽妃于氏，為徽表訟，詔付丞相高陽王雍等宗室議決其罪，以王還第。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Director within the Palace, but before assuming the post he was convicted of violating Lady Yu, consort of Prince Chengyang of Hui; Prince Hui memorialized accusing him; an edict referred the case to the Chief Minister Prince of Gaoyang, Yong, and other royal kin to decide his crime, and he was sent back to his mansion as a prince.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Director within the Palace, but before assuming the post he was convicted of violating Lady Yu, consort of Prince Chengyang of Hui; Prince Hui memorialized accusing him; an edict referred the case to the Chief Minister Prince of Gaoyang, Yong, and other royal kin to decide his crime, and he was sent back to his mansion as a prince.

sentences.zh: 及沃野鎮人破六韓拔陵反叛，臨淮王彧討之，失利，詔深為北道大都督，[19]受尚書令李崇節度。

translations.literal: When the people of Woye Garrison, Poliuhan Baling, rebelled, Prince Linhuai of Yu campaigned against them and failed; an edict made Shen Grand Commander of the Northern Route,[19] subject to the command of Director of the Secretariat Li Chong.
translations.idiomatic: When the people of Woye Garrison, Poliuhan Baling, rebelled, Prince Linhuai of Yu campaigned against them and failed; an edict made Shen Grand Commander of the Northern Route,[19] subject to the command of Director of the Secretariat Li Chong.

sentences.zh: 時東道都督崔暹敗於白道，[20]深上書曰：

translations.literal: At that time Eastern Route Commander Cui Xuan was defeated at White Road;[20] Shen submitted a memorial:
translations.idiomatic: At that time Eastern Route Commander Cui Xuan was defeated at White Road;[20] Shen submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 邊豎構逆，以成紛梗，其所由來，非一朝也。

translations.literal: Border villains have raised rebellion and formed disorder; its causes did not arise in a single morning.
translations.idiomatic: Border villains have raised rebellion and formed disorder; its causes did not arise in a single morning.

sentences.zh: 昔皇始以移防為重，盛簡親賢，擁麾作鎮，配以高門子弟，以死防遏，不但不廢仕宦，至乃偏得復除。

translations.literal: In antiquity, at Huangshi, shifting garrisons was held important; they carefully chose kin and worthies, grasped banners and served as commandants, paired with sons of eminent houses who would die blocking the frontier — not only were they not removed from office, they even received special exemption privileges.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, at Huangshi, shifting garrisons was held important; they carefully chose kin and worthies, grasped banners and served as commandants, paired with sons of eminent houses who would die blocking the frontier — not only were they not removed from office, they even received special exemption privileges.

sentences.zh: 當時人物，忻慕為之。

translations.literal: Men of that time admired this and aspired to it.
translations.idiomatic: Men of that time admired this and aspired to it.

sentences.zh: 及太和在歷，僕射李沖當官任事，涼州土人，悉免厮役，豐沛舊門，仍防邊戍。

translations.literal: When the Taihe era came, Vice Director Li Chong held office and managed affairs: natives of Liang Province were all exempted from menial service, while the old families of Feng and Pei still guarded the border garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taihe era came, Vice Director Li Chong held office and managed affairs: natives of Liang Province were all exempted from menial service, while the old families of Feng and Pei still guarded the border garrisons.

sentences.zh: 自非得罪當世，莫肯與之為伍。

translations.literal: Unless one had offended the age, none would join them.
translations.idiomatic: Unless one had offended the age, none would join them.

sentences.zh: 征鎮驅使，但為虞候白直，一生推遷，不過軍主。

translations.literal: The frontier garrisons employed them only as scouts and runners; advancement in a lifetime went no higher than garrison chief.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier garrisons employed them only as scouts and runners; advancement in a lifetime went no higher than garrison chief.

sentences.zh: 然其往世房分留居京者得上品通官，在鎮者便為清途所隔。

translations.literal: Yet branches of their clans that remained in the capital in former generations could obtain high-ranking regular offices, while those at the garrisons were shut off from the clear path of advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Yet branches of their clans that remained in the capital in former generations could obtain high-ranking regular offices, while those at the garrisons were shut off from the clear path of advancement.

sentences.zh: 或投彼有北，以御魑魅，多復逃胡鄉。

translations.literal: Some fled to the northern wastes to escape demons; many again fled to barbarian villages.
translations.idiomatic: Some fled to the northern wastes to escape demons; many again fled to barbarian villages.

sentences.zh: 乃峻邊兵之格，鎮人浮遊在外，皆聽流兵捉之。

translations.literal: Then the standards for border troops were made harsh; garrison men drifting outside were all subject to capture by roving patrols.
translations.idiomatic: Then the standards for border troops were made harsh; garrison men drifting outside were all subject to capture by roving patrols.

sentences.zh: 於是少年不得從師，長者不得遊宦，獨為匪人，言者流涕。

translations.literal: Thereupon youths could not follow teachers, elders could not seek office abroad — they alone were made outlaws, and those who spoke of it wept.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon youths could not follow teachers, elders could not seek office abroad — they alone were made outlaws, and those who spoke of it wept.

sentences.zh: 自定鼎伊洛，邊任益輕，唯底滯凡才，出為鎮將，轉相模習，專事聚斂。

translations.literal: From the time the capital was fixed at Yiluo, border posts grew ever lighter; only stagnant mediocrity was sent out as garrison commanders, each imitating the other, devoted solely to amassing wealth.
translations.idiomatic: From the time the capital was fixed at Yiluo, border posts grew ever lighter; only stagnant mediocrity was sent out as garrison commanders, each imitating the other, devoted solely to amassing wealth.

sentences.zh: 或有諸方姦吏，犯罪配邊，為之指蹤，過弄官府，政以賄立，莫能自改。

translations.literal: Some corrupt officials from various regions, convicted and assigned to the border, charted their tracks for them and toyed with the government offices; government was established through bribes, and none could reform themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Some corrupt officials from various regions, convicted and assigned to the border, charted their tracks for them and toyed with the government offices; government was established through bribes, and none could reform themselves.

sentences.zh: 咸言姦吏為此，無不切齒憎怒。

translations.literal: All said corrupt officials did this, and none failed to gnash teeth in hatred.
translations.idiomatic: All said corrupt officials did this, and none failed to gnash teeth in hatred.

sentences.zh: 及阿那瓌背恩，縱掠竊奔，命師追之，十五萬眾度沙漠，不日而還。

translations.literal: When Anagui betrayed his favor, plundered, and fled in secret, the court ordered armies in pursuit; one hundred fifty thousand men crossed the desert and returned within days.
translations.idiomatic: When Anagui betrayed his favor, plundered, and fled in secret, the court ordered armies in pursuit; one hundred fifty thousand men crossed the desert and returned within days.

sentences.zh: 邊人見此援師，便自意輕中國。

translations.literal: The border people, seeing such relief troops, themselves conceived a light estimate of China.
translations.idiomatic: The border people, seeing such relief troops, themselves conceived a light estimate of China.

sentences.zh: 尚書令臣崇時即申聞，求改鎮為州，將允其願，抑亦先覺。

translations.literal: Minister of State Chong then immediately reported it, asking to change garrisons into provinces — a wish about to be granted, and also a foresight.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of State Chong then immediately reported it, asking to change garrisons into provinces — a wish about to be granted, and also a foresight.

sentences.zh: 朝廷未許。

translations.literal: The court did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not permit it.

sentences.zh: 而高闕戍主率下失和，拔陵殺之，敢為逆命，[21]攻城掠地，所見必誅。

translations.literal: But the garrison chief at Gaogue lost harmony with his men; Baling killed him and dared to take treasonous command;[21] attacking cities and seizing land, wherever he went he slew.
translations.idiomatic: But the garrison chief at Gaogue lost harmony with his men; Baling killed him and dared to take treasonous command;[21] attacking cities and seizing land, wherever he went he slew.

sentences.zh: 王師屢北，賊黨日盛。

translations.literal: The royal armies repeatedly suffered defeat in the north; the rebel party grew daily stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial forces were beaten again and again in the north, and the rebels grew stronger by the day.

sentences.zh: 此段之舉，指望銷平。

translations.literal: This expedition was undertaken in hope of extinguishing and pacifying them.
translations.idiomatic: This campaign was meant to crush the rebellion and restore order.

sentences.zh: 其崔暹隻輪不反，臣崇與臣逡巡復路。

translations.literal: As for Cui Xian, not even one wheel returned; Chong and your servant withdrew along the road in hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xian was wiped out to a man; Li Chong and I fell back along the road in retreat.

sentences.zh: 今者相與還次雲中，馬首是瞻，未便西邁，將士之情，莫不解體。

translations.literal: Now we have together returned and encamped at Yunzhong; all eyes watch the horse's head, and we have not yet advanced west; the officers' and soldiers' feelings are entirely without cohesion.
translations.idiomatic: We have fallen back to Yunzhong together; the whole army hangs on your will, yet we cannot march west, and the troops' morale has utterly collapsed.

sentences.zh: 今日所慮，非止西北，將恐諸鎮尋亦如此，天下之事，何易可量。

translations.literal: What we worry over today is not only the northwest; we fear that the various garrisons will soon do likewise — how easily can affairs under Heaven be measured?
translations.idiomatic: Today's fear is not only for the northwest; soon every garrison may follow suit. Who can fathom what will become of the realm?

sentences.zh: 時不納其策。

translations.literal: The court at that time did not accept his plan.
translations.idiomatic: The court rejected his proposal.

sentences.zh: 東西部敕勒之叛，朝議更思深言，遣兼黃門侍郎酈道元為大使，欲復鎮為州，以順人望。

translations.literal: When the eastern and western Tiele rebelled, court deliberation again recalled Shen's words; they dispatched Concurrent Palace Attendant Li Daoyuan as chief envoy, intending to restore garrisons to provinces, to accord with men's hopes.
translations.idiomatic: After the eastern and western Tiele rose in revolt, the court reconsidered Shen's advice and sent Concurrent Palace Attendant Li Daoyuan as grand envoy to convert the garrisons back into provinces and satisfy popular expectation.

sentences.zh: 會六鎮盡叛，不得施行。

translations.literal: But it happened that all six garrisons rebelled entirely, and it could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Before the plan could be enacted, all six garrisons had rebelled.

sentences.zh: 深後上言：「今六鎮俱叛，二部高車，亦同惡黨，以疲兵討之，不必制敵。

translations.literal: Shen later submitted a memorial: "Now all six garrisons have rebelled; the two divisions of Gaoche likewise share the same evil party — to attack them with weary troops will not necessarily overcome the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Shen memorialized again: "All six garrisons are in revolt, and the two Gaoche confederacies are allied with them. Exhausted troops cannot be relied on to defeat the enemy.

sentences.zh: 請簡選兵，或留守恒州要處，更為後圖。」

translations.literal: I ask to select elite troops, or to hold the strategic points of Heng Province, and make fresh plans thereafter."
translations.idiomatic: Select picked troops and either hold the vital points around Heng Province or devise another plan."

sentences.zh: 及李崇徵還，深專總戎政。

translations.literal: When Li Chong was recalled from campaign, Shen alone held overall military authority.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Chong was recalled from the field, Shen alone held overall military command.

sentences.zh: 拔陵避蠕蠕，南移渡河。

translations.literal: Baling, avoiding the Rouran, shifted south across the river.
translations.idiomatic: Baling, evading the Rouran, moved south across the river.

sentences.zh: 先是，別將李叔仁以拔陵來逼，請求迎援，深赴之，前後降附二十萬人。

translations.literal: Earlier, Assistant General Li Shuren, pressed by Baling, had requested relief; Shen went to his aid, and before and after, two hundred thousand submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Assistant General Li Shuren, harried by Baling, had asked for reinforcements; Shen marched to relieve him, and in all two hundred thousand people surrendered.

sentences.zh: 深與行臺元纂表求恒州北別立郡縣，安置降戶，隨宜賑賚，息其亂心。

translations.literal: Shen and the Mobile Court Yuan Zuan memorialized asking to establish separate commanderies and counties north of Heng Province to settle the surrendered households, grant relief as appropriate, and quiet their rebellious minds.
translations.idiomatic: Shen and the mobile court commissioner Yuan Zuan asked to set up separate commanderies and counties north of Heng Province to resettle the surrendered households, grant relief as needed, and calm their rebellious hearts.

sentences.zh: 不從，詔遣黃門郎楊昱分散之於冀、定、瀛三州就食。

translations.literal: The court did not agree and ordered Palace Attendant Yang Yu to disperse them among Ji, Ding, and Ying provinces to find food.
translations.idiomatic: The court refused and ordered Palace Attendant Yang Yu to scatter them through Ji, Ding, and Ying provinces to find sustenance.

sentences.zh: [22]深謂纂曰：「此輩復為乞活矣，禍亂當由此作。

translations.literal: [22] Shen said to Zuan: "These people will again become those begging to live; disorder will arise from this.
translations.idiomatic: [22] Shen told Zuan, "They will become refugees begging to live again — trouble will start here.

sentences.zh: 」既而鮮于脩禮叛於定州，杜洛周反於幽州，其餘降戶，猶在恒州，遂欲推深為主。

translations.literal: Before long Xianyu Xiuli rebelled at Ding Province and Du Luozhou rose in You Province; the remaining surrendered households still at Heng Province then wished to make Shen their leader.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xianyu Xiuli rebelled in Ding Province and Du Luozhou in You Province; the surrendered households still at Heng Province then tried to make Shen their leader.

sentences.zh: 深乃上書乞還京師，令左衞將軍楊津代深為都督，以深為侍中、右衞將軍、定州刺史。

translations.literal: Shen thereupon memorialized begging return to the capital; he had Left Guard General Yang Jin replace him as commander, and Shen was made Palace Attendant, Right Guard General, and Administrator of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: Shen then asked to return to the capital, had Left Guard General Yang Jin replace him as commander, and was appointed Palace Attendant, Right Guard General, and Administrator of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 時中山太守趙叔隆、別駕崔融討賊失利，臺使劉審考覈，未訖，會賊逼中山，深乃令叔隆防境。

translations.literal: At that time Administrator of Zhongshan Zhao Shulong and Vice-Prefect Cui Rong had failed in attacking the bandits; court envoy Liu Shen was examining the case but it was not finished when the bandits pressed Zhongshan; Shen then ordered Shulong to guard the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The Administrator of Zhongshan, Zhao Shulong, and Vice-Prefect Cui Rong had been defeated by the rebels; court envoy Liu Shen was still investigating when the rebels threatened Zhongshan, and Shen ordered Shulong to hold the border.

sentences.zh: 審馳驛還京，云深擅相放縱。

translations.literal: Liu Shen galloped by post-station relay back to the capital, reporting that Shen had presumptuously released and indulged them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shen raced back to the capital by relay and reported that Shen had overstepped his authority and let them go free.

sentences.zh: 城陽王徽與深有隙，因此構之，乃徵深為吏部尚書，兼中領軍。

translations.literal: Prince Yangyang Hui bore a grudge against Shen; exploiting this, he framed him, and Shen was summoned as Minister of the Civil Service and Concurrent Commander of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yangyang Hui, who bore a grudge against Shen, used the charge to frame him; Shen was recalled as Minister of the Civil Service and concurrent Commander of the Central Army.

sentences.zh: 及深至都，肅宗不欲使徽深相憾，敕因宴會令相和解。

translations.literal: When Shen reached the capital, Emperor Xiaozong did not wish Hui and Shen to remain at odds and ordered that at a banquet they reconcile.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen reached the capital, Emperor Xiaozong did not want Hui and Shen to remain enemies and ordered them to reconcile at a banquet.

sentences.zh: 徽銜不已。

translations.literal: Hui nursed resentment without end.
translations.idiomatic: Hui nursed his resentment without end.

sentences.zh: 後河間王琛等為鮮于脩禮所敗，乃除深儀同三司、大都督，章武王融為左都督，裴衍為右都督，並受深節度。

translations.literal: Later, when Prince Hejian Chen and others were defeated by Xianyu Xiuli, Shen was appointed Supervisor of the Left, Grand Commander; Prince Zhangwu Rong was Left Commander and Pei Yan Right Commander — all under Shen's direction.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after Prince Hejian Chen and others were defeated by Xianyu Xiuli, Shen was made Supervisor of the Left and Grand Commander; Prince Zhangwu Rong became Left Commander and Pei Yan Right Commander, both under Shen's command.

sentences.zh: 徽因奏靈太后構深曰：「廣陽以愛子握兵在外，不可測也。

translations.literal: Hui thereupon memorialized to Empress Dowager Ling to frame Shen: "Guangyang holds troops abroad through a beloved son — he cannot be measured.
translations.idiomatic: Hui then memorialized Empress Dowager Ling to slander Shen: "Guangyang has his beloved son commanding troops abroad — he is unpredictable.

sentences.zh: 」乃敕章武王等潛相防備。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered Prince Zhangwu and the others covertly to guard against one another.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict secretly ordered Prince Zhangwu and the others to guard against him.

sentences.zh: 融遂以敕示深，深懼，事無大小，不敢自決。

translations.literal: Rong then showed the edict to Shen; Shen was afraid, and in matters great and small dared not decide on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Rong showed the edict to Shen; Shen was terrified and dared not decide anything, great or small, on his own.

sentences.zh: 靈太后聞之，乃使問深意狀。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling heard of it, she sent to question Shen on the true circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling heard of this, she sent to ask Shen for a full account.

sentences.zh: 乃具言曰：

translations.literal: He then set forth in full, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He then laid out the whole case, saying:

sentences.zh: 往者元叉執權，移天徙日，而徽託附，無翼而飛。

translations.literal: In the past Yuan Cha held power, moving Heaven and shifting the sun, yet Hui attached himself and flew without wings.
translations.idiomatic: In the old days Yuan Cha held power and turned the world upside down, yet Hui attached himself to him and rose without wings.

sentences.zh: 今大明反政，任寄唯重，以徽褊心，銜臣切骨。

translations.literal: Now the great bright throne has restored government; his commissions are weighty alone — because of Hui's narrow heart, he harbors hatred for your servant to the bone.
translations.idiomatic: Now that enlightened rule has been restored, he alone holds the heaviest trust; but Hui's petty heart nurses a hatred for me that cuts to the bone.

sentences.zh: 臣以疏滯，遠離京輦，被其構阻，無所不為。

translations.literal: Your servant, being coarse and stagnant, was far from the imperial carriage and was blocked by his machinations; there was nothing he would not do.
translations.idiomatic: I am slow and undistinguished, far from the capital, and he has blocked me with intrigue at every turn.

sentences.zh: 然臣昔不在其後，自此以來，翻成陵谷。

translations.literal: Yet your servant was not formerly in his rear; since then the heights and valleys have reversed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I was not formerly behind him; since then fortunes have reversed like mountain and valley.

sentences.zh: 徽遂一歲八遷，位居宰相；

translations.literal: Hui then moved eight times in one year, standing in the place of chief minister;
translations.idiomatic: Hui was promoted eight times in a single year and stood as chief minister;

sentences.zh: 臣乃積年淹滯，有功不錄。

translations.literal: your servant was stalled for accumulated years, with merit unrecorded.
translations.idiomatic: while I languished for years with my merits unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 自徽執政以來，非但抑臣而已，北征之勳，皆被擁塞。

translations.literal: Since Hui took power, it was not only your servant who was suppressed — northern campaign merits were all choked off.
translations.idiomatic: Since Hui took power, he has suppressed not only me but every merit won on the northern campaigns.

sentences.zh: 將士告捷，終無片賞。

translations.literal: When officers and soldiers reported victory, in the end there was not a shred of reward.
translations.idiomatic: When officers and soldiers reported victory, they received not a shred of reward.

sentences.zh: 雖為表請，多不蒙遂。

translations.literal: Though memorials were made, mostly they were not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Though memorials were submitted, most requests went ungranted.

sentences.zh: 前留元標據于盛樂，後被重圍，析骸易子，倒懸一隅，嬰城二載。

translations.literal: Earlier Yuan Biao was left holding Shengle, later was heavily besieged — splitting flesh and exchanging children, hanging upside down in a corner, defending the city for two years.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yuan Biao was left to hold Shengle and later was tightly besieged — families split flesh and exchanged children, trapped in desperate straits, and held the city for two years.

sentences.zh: 賊散之後，依階乞官，徽乃盤退，不允所請。

translations.literal: After the bandits dispersed, he sought office by rank; Hui then stalled and retreated, not granting what was requested.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels dispersed, he petitioned for office by seniority; Hui obstructed him and refused what he asked.

sentences.zh: 而徐州下邳戍主賈勳，法僧叛後，暫被圍逼，固守之勳，比之未重，乃立得州，即授開國。

translations.literal: Yet Jia Xun, garrison chief at Xiapi in Xuzhou, after Faseng's rebellion was briefly besieged — his merit in firm defense, compared with Biao's, was not heavier, yet he immediately received a province and was enfeoffed as a state founder.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Jia Xun, garrison chief at Xiapi in Xuzhou, was only briefly besieged after Faseng's rebellion; his defense was nothing beside Biao's, yet he was made a provincial governor at once and enfeoffed as state founder.

sentences.zh: 天下之事，其流一也，功同賞異，不平謂何。

translations.literal: Affairs under Heaven run in one channel — equal merit but unequal rewards: how can this be called fair?
translations.idiomatic: Under Heaven the rule is one: equal merit but unequal reward — where is the fairness in that?

sentences.zh: 又驃騎李崇，北征之日，啟募八州之人，聽用關西之格。

translations.literal: Moreover Grand General Li Chong, on the day of the northern expedition, proposed recruiting men from eight provinces, allowing use of the Guanxi scale of reward.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Li Chong, when the northern expedition set out, proposed recruiting from eight provinces and applying the Guanxi reward scale.

sentences.zh: 及臣在後，依此科賞，復言北道征者不得同於關西。

translations.literal: When your servant was behind, rewards were given by this statute — then he said that northern-route campaigners could not be treated the same as Guanxi.
translations.idiomatic: When I served in the rear, rewards followed that standard — then he said northern-route soldiers could not be treated like those of Guanxi.

sentences.zh: 定襄陵廟之至重，平城守國之要鎮，若計此而論，功亦何負於秦楚？

translations.literal: Dingxiang's imperial tombs are of the utmost weight; Pingcheng is the vital bastion guarding the state — if one reckons by this, what merit falls short of Qin and Chu?
translations.idiomatic: The imperial tombs at Dingxiang and the capital bastion at Pingcheng are matters of the highest weight — judged by that, how did our merit fall short of Qin and Chu?

sentences.zh: 但以嫉臣之故，便欲望風排抑。

translations.literal: But solely because of hatred for your servant, he wished to bow them down before the wind.
translations.idiomatic: But solely from hatred of me, he tried to crush them at a breath.

sentences.zh: 然其當途以來，何直退勳而已，但是隨臣征者，即便為所嫉。

translations.literal: Yet since he held the road of power, it was not only advancing merits that were set back — whoever campaigned with your servant was at once his object of jealousy.
translations.idiomatic: Since he took power, it was not only my promotions he blocked — anyone who campaigned with me became his target of jealousy.

sentences.zh: 統軍袁叔和曾經省訴，徽初言有理，又聞北征隸臣為統，應時變色。

translations.literal: Army Commander Yuan Shuhe once appealed at the ministry; Hui at first said it was reasonable, then hearing that on the northern expedition he would serve under your servant as commander, instantly changed color.
translations.idiomatic: Army Commander Yuan Shuhe once appealed to the ministry; Hui at first said he was in the right, but when he heard that on the northern expedition he would serve under me, his face changed on the spot.

sentences.zh: 復令臣兄子仲顯異端訟臣，緝緝翩翩，謀相誹謗。

translations.literal: He again had your servant's elder brother's son Zhongxian bring a strange suit against your servant — bustling and flitting, plotting mutual slander.
translations.idiomatic: He again had my elder brother's son Zhongxian bring a strange suit against me — whispering and plotting slander together.

sentences.zh: 言臣惡者，接以恩顏；

translations.literal: Those who spoke of your servant's evil he met with a gracious countenance;
translations.idiomatic: Those who spoke ill of me he greeted with kindness;

sentences.zh: 稱臣善者，即被嫌責。

translations.literal: those who praised your servant's good were at once suspected and blamed.
translations.idiomatic: those who praised me he at once suspected and blamed.

sentences.zh: 甄琛曾理臣屈，乃視之若仇讎；

translations.literal: Zhen Chen once redressed your servant's grievance, yet he treated him like a foe;
translations.idiomatic: Zhen Chen once redressed my grievance, yet Hui treated him like an enemy;

sentences.zh: 徐紇頗言臣短，即待之如親戚。

translations.literal: Xu He often spoke of your servant's faults, yet he treated him like kin.
translations.idiomatic: Xu He often spoke of my faults, yet Hui treated him like kin.

sentences.zh: 又驃騎長史祖瑩，昔在軍中，妄增首級，矯亂戎行，蠹害軍府，獲罪有司，避命山澤。

translations.literal: Moreover Grand General Chief Clerk Zu Ying, formerly in the army, falsely inflated head-counts, perverted military order, harmed the military headquarters, and was guilty before the authorities; he fled his fate in mountains and marshes.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Chief Clerk Zu Ying, while in the army, had falsely inflated head-counts, perverted military order, and harmed the headquarters; found guilty by the authorities, he fled into the hills.

sentences.zh: 直以謗臣之故，徽乃還雪其罪。

translations.literal: Solely because of slandering your servant, Hui then cleared his crime.
translations.idiomatic: Solely for slandering me, Hui cleared his crime.

sentences.zh: 臣府司馬劉敬，比送降人，既到定州，翻然背叛。

translations.literal: Your servant's headquarters Marshal Liu Jing, who lately escorted surrendered men, once they reached Ding Province, abruptly rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: My headquarters marshal Liu Jing, who had lately escorted surrendered men, rebelled as soon as they reached Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 賊如決河，豈其能擁。

translations.literal: The bandits were like a burst river — how could he contain them?
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were like a river breaking its banks — how could he hold them?

sentences.zh: 且以臣府參僚，不免身首異處。

translations.literal: Moreover, as staff of your servant's headquarters, he did not escape death in different places for head and trunk.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, as staff of my headquarters, we did not escape losing our heads.

sentences.zh: 徽既怒遷，捨其元惡。

translations.literal: Hui was angry and shifted blame, letting go the chief culprit.
translations.idiomatic: Hui, angry, shifted the blame and let the chief culprit go.

translations.literal: The text is deficient.
translations.idiomatic: The source text is missing at this point.

sentences.zh: 及胥徒。

translations.literal: and the clerks and runners.
translations.idiomatic: And to the clerks and runners as well.

sentences.zh: 從臣行者莫不悚懼。

translations.literal: Those who accompanied your servant on the road were all fearful and trembling.
translations.idiomatic: Those who traveled with me were all terrified.

sentences.zh: 頃恒州之人，乞臣為刺史，徽乃斐然言不可測。

translations.literal: Recently the people of Heng Province begged that your servant be their administrator; Hui then grandly spoke of immeasurability.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the people of Heng Province asked that I be made their administrator; Hui grandly called me unpredictable.

sentences.zh: 及降戶結謀，臣頻表啟，徽乃因執言此事。

translations.literal: When the surrendered households plotted, your servant repeatedly memorialized; Hui then seized on this matter and spoke of it.
translations.idiomatic: When the surrendered households plotted, I memorialized repeatedly; Hui seized on the matter and denounced me.

sentences.zh: 及向定州，遠彼姦惡，又復論臣將有異志。

translations.literal: When heading to Ding Province, far from those wicked men, he again discussed that your servant harbored rebellious intent.
translations.idiomatic: When I marched to Ding Province, far from those villains, he again claimed I harbored rebellious intent.

sentences.zh: 翻覆如此，欲相陷沒。

translations.literal: Reversing thus, he wished to trap and destroy your servant.
translations.idiomatic: Reversing himself thus, he meant to trap and destroy me.

sentences.zh: 致令國朝遽賜遷代。

translations.literal: This caused the court hastily to grant transfer and replacement.
translations.idiomatic: That is what made the court hastily transfer and replace me.

sentences.zh: 賊起之由，誰使然也？

translations.literal: The cause of the bandits' rise — who made it so?
translations.idiomatic: Who made the rebels rise in the first place?

sentences.zh: 徽既優幸，任隆一世，慕勢之徒，於臣何有。

translations.literal: Hui, being favored and privileged, held rank towering for a generation; those who court power — what do they owe your servant?
translations.idiomatic: Hui, favored and privileged, towered over a generation; what did power-seekers owe me?

sentences.zh: 是故餘人攝選，車馬填門，及臣居邊，賓遊罕至。

translations.literal: Therefore when others held appointments, carriages and horses filled the gates; when your servant dwelt on the frontier, guests and visitors rarely came.
translations.idiomatic: So when others held office, carriages and horses filled their gates; when I served on the frontier, guests scarcely came.

sentences.zh: 臣近比為慮其為梗，是以孜孜乞赴京闕。

translations.literal: Your servant lately feared he would be an obstruction, and thus earnestly begged to go to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: I lately feared he would obstruct me and earnestly begged to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 屬流人舉斧，元戎垂翅，復從後命，自安無所，僶俛先驅，不敢辭事。

translations.literal: Just then displaced people raised axes, the commander-in-chief folded his wings; again following the later command, with nowhere to rest secure, your servant bent low as vanguard, not daring to decline the task.
translations.idiomatic: Just then refugees took up arms and the supreme commander was beaten down; obeying the later order with nowhere to rest, I bent low as vanguard and did not dare refuse the task.

sentences.zh: 及臣出都，行塵未滅，已聞在後復生異議。

translations.literal: When your servant left the capital, the dust of travel had not yet settled when already word came that behind him fresh dissent had arisen.
translations.idiomatic: When I left the capital, the dust of my departure had not settled before fresh accusations arose behind me.

sentences.zh: 言臣將兒自隨，證為可疑之兆，忽稱此以構亂。

translations.literal: Saying your servant brought his sons along — proof of a suspicious omen — suddenly using this to frame rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: They said I took my sons with me — proof of suspicious intent — and suddenly used this to frame me for rebellion.

sentences.zh: 悠悠之人，復傳音響，言左軍臣融、右軍臣衍，皆受密敕，伺察臣事。

translations.literal: Idle people again spread rumors, saying Left Army your servant Rong and Right Army your servant Yan had all received secret edicts to watch your servant's conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Idle people spread rumors that Left Army Commander Rong and Right Army Commander Yan had secret orders to watch my every move.

sentences.zh: 徽既用心如此，臣將何以自安！

translations.literal: Hui having used his heart thus, how can your servant find security!
translations.idiomatic: With Hui's mind set thus, how can I feel secure!

sentences.zh: 竊以天步未夷，國難猶梗，方伯之任，於斯為急。

translations.literal: Your servant ventures to think the heavenly steps are not yet pacified, national difficulty still blocks the way — the charge of regional lords is urgent at this juncture.
translations.idiomatic: I venture to think the realm is not yet pacified and national peril still blocks the way — the post of regional commander is urgent now.

sentences.zh: 徽昔臨藩，乃有人譽，及居端右，蔑爾無聞。

translations.literal: Hui when he governed a fief had some human repute; once he stood at the top, there was nothing heard of him.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui governed a fief he had some reputation; once he stood at court center, nothing was heard of him.

sentences.zh: 今求出之為州，使得申其利用。

translations.literal: Now I ask that he be sent out as administrator of a province, that he may exert his usefulness.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that he now be sent out to govern a province where he can put his talents to use.

sentences.zh: 徽若外從所長，臣無內慮之切。

translations.literal: If Hui outwardly follows his strengths, your servant will have no keen inner worry.
translations.idiomatic: If Hui is sent out to do what he does best, I shall have no gnawing fear within.

sentences.zh: 脫蒙。

translations.literal: If I may receive [favor].
translations.idiomatic: If I may receive [your favor].

translations.literal: The text is deficient.
translations.idiomatic: The source text is missing at this point.

sentences.zh: 公私幸甚。

translations.literal: great fortune for public and private.
translations.idiomatic: It will be great fortune for public and private alike.

sentences.zh: 深以兵士頻經退散，人無鬬情，連營轉柵，日行十里。

translations.literal: Shen, because the troops had repeatedly been routed and scattered and men lacked fighting spirit, moved camp after camp shifting palisades, advancing ten li a day.
translations.idiomatic: Because the troops had been routed again and again and men had lost the will to fight, Shen moved camp by camp, shifting palisades, and advanced only ten li a day.

sentences.zh: 行達交津，隔水而陳。

translations.literal: Marching to Jiaojin, they drew up across the water.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Jiaojin, they drew up their lines across the water.

sentences.zh: 賊脩禮常與葛榮謀，後稍信朔州人毛普賢，榮常銜之。

translations.literal: The bandit Xiuli often plotted with Ge Rong; later he came slightly to trust Mao Puxian of Shuozhou, and Rong constantly resented it.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Xiuli often plotted with Ge Rong; later he came to trust Mao Puxian of Shuozhou, and Rong nursed a grudge.

sentences.zh: 普賢昔為深統軍，及在交津，深使人諭之，普賢乃有降意。

translations.literal: Puxian had formerly been Shen's army commander; when at Jiaojin, Shen sent men to persuade him, and Puxian then had intent to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Puxian had once served as Shen's army commander; at Jiaojin Shen sent men to win him over, and Puxian was ready to surrender.

sentences.zh: 又使錄事參軍元晏說賊程殺鬼，果相猜貳，葛榮遂殺普賢、脩禮而自立。

translations.literal: He also sent Recorder of Affairs Yuan Yan to speak to the bandit Cheng Shaygui; sure enough mutual suspicion arose, and Ge Rong then killed Puxian and Xiuli and set himself up alone.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Recorder of Affairs Yuan Yan to sway the rebel Cheng Shaygui; suspicion took hold between them, and Ge Rong killed Puxian and Xiuli and made himself leader.

sentences.zh: 榮以新得大眾，上下未安，遂北度瀛州，深便率眾北轉。

translations.literal: Rong, having newly acquired a great host, was not secure above and below, and thereupon crossed north over Ying Province; Shen then led his host to turn north.
translations.idiomatic: Rong, having just taken command of a huge force, was not yet secure in his rule and marched north across Ying Province; Shen then led his troops north.

sentences.zh: 榮東攻章武王融，戰敗於白牛邏。

translations.literal: Rong attacked east against Prince Zhangwu Rong and was defeated at Bainiuluo.
translations.idiomatic: Rong attacked east against Prince Zhangwu Rong and was defeated at Bainiuluo.

sentences.zh: [23]深遂退走，趨定州。

translations.literal: [23] Shen then retreated fleeing, hurrying to Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: [23] Shen then fled in retreat toward Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 聞刺史楊津疑其有異志，乃止於州南佛寺。

translations.literal: Hearing that Administrator Yang Jin suspected him of rebellious intent, he halted at a Buddhist temple south of the province.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Administrator Yang Jin suspected him of disloyalty, he stopped at a Buddhist temple south of the city.

sentences.zh: 停三日夜，乃召都督毛諡等六七人，臂肩為約，危難之際，期相拯恤。

translations.literal: Halting three days and nights, he then summoned Commanders Mao Yi and six or seven others, linking arms in covenant — in time of peril, they pledged mutual rescue.
translations.idiomatic: After three days and nights he summoned Commanders Mao Yi and six or seven others, linked arms in covenant, and pledged to save one another in peril.

sentences.zh: 諡疑深意異，乃密告津云，深謀不軌。

translations.literal: Yi suspected Shen's intent was strange and secretly told Jin that Shen plotted treason.
translations.idiomatic: Yi suspected Shen's intentions, secretly reported to Jin that Shen plotted treason.

sentences.zh: 津遣諡討深，深走出，諡叫噪追躡。

translations.literal: Jin sent Yi to attack Shen; Shen fled out, and Yi shouted and chased close behind.
translations.idiomatic: Jin sent Yi against Shen; Shen fled, and Yi shouted and pursued close behind.

sentences.zh: 深與左右行至博陵郡界，逢賊遊騎，乃引詣葛榮。

translations.literal: Shen with his attendants went to the border of Boling commandery, met bandit scouts, and was led to Ge Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Shen and his attendants reached the border of Boling commandery, met rebel scouts, and were taken to Ge Rong.

sentences.zh: 賊徒見深，頗有喜者。

translations.literal: Among the bandit followers who saw Shen, many were pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Many of the rebels who saw Shen were glad.

sentences.zh: 榮新自立，內惡之，乃害深。

translations.literal: Rong, newly established himself, inwardly hated him, and thereupon killed Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Rong, having just seized power, hated him inwardly and killed him.

sentences.zh: 莊帝追復王爵，贈司徒公，諡曰忠武。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang posthumously restored his princely title, conferred Minister of State, and gave the posthumous name Loyal-Warlike.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang posthumously restored his princely title, made him Minister of State, and gave him the posthumous name Loyal-Warlike.

sentences.zh: 湛弟瑾，尚書祠部郎。

translations.literal: Zhan's younger brother Jin was Director in the Ministry of Rites for the Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan's younger brother Jin served as Director of the Ancestral Temple Office in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 後謀殺齊文襄，事泄，合門伏法。

translations.literal: Later he plotted to kill Qi Wenxiang; the matter leaked; the whole household suffered execution by law.
translations.idiomatic: Later he plotted against Qi Wenxiang; when the plot leaked, his entire household was executed.

sentences.zh: 湛子法輪，紫光所生也。

translations.literal: Zhan's son Falun was born to Ziguang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan's son Falun was born to Lady Ziguang.

sentences.zh: 齊王矜湛覆滅，乃啟原之，復其爵土。

translations.literal: The Qi king pitied Zhan's annihilation and thereupon petitioned to restore him, recovering his noble rank and fief.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi king, pitying Zhan's destruction, petitioned for his restoration and returned his title and fief.

sentences.zh: 南安王余，真君三年封吳王，後改封南安王。

translations.literal: Prince Yu of Nan'an — in the third year of Zhenjun was enfeoffed Prince of Wu; later his title was changed to Prince of Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yu of Nan'an was enfeoffed as Prince of Wu in the third year of Zhenjun and later renamed Prince of Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 世祖暴崩，中常侍宗愛矯皇太后令迎余而立之，然後發喪。

translations.literal: When Shizu suddenly died, Palace Attendant Zong Ai forged the empress dowager's order to welcome Yu and establish him, and only then announced the death.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu died suddenly, the eunuch Zong Ai forged an empress-dowager order to bring Yu to court and install him before the death was announced.

sentences.zh: 大赦，改年為永平。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed; the reign era was changed to Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: The court proclaimed a general amnesty and adopted the reign title Yongping.

sentences.zh: 余自以非次而立，厚賞羣下，取悅於眾。

translations.literal: Yu, considering himself established out of proper order, richly rewarded subordinates to win favor from the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he had seized the throne out of turn, Yu lavished rewards on his followers to win popular favor.

sentences.zh: 為長夜之飲，聲樂不絕，旬月之間，帑藏空罄。

translations.literal: He held long-night feasts; music never ceased; within a month the treasury was empty.
translations.idiomatic: He threw endless night-long feasts with ceaseless music, and within a month the treasury was drained.

sentences.zh: 尤好弋獵，出入無度，邊方告難，余不恤之，百姓憤惋，而余晏如也。

translations.literal: He especially loved hawking; went out and in without measure; the border reported distress but Yu did not pity it; the people were angry and grieved, yet Yu was at ease as before.
translations.idiomatic: He loved hunting above all and came and went without restraint. Border alarms went unheeded; the people seethed with anger, yet Yu remained unruffled.

sentences.zh: 宗愛權恣日甚，內外憚之。

translations.literal: Zong Ai's power grew daily more reckless; inside and outside feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Ai's power grew daily more lawless, and court and realm alike feared him.

sentences.zh: 余疑愛將謀變，奪其權，愛怒，因余祭廟，夜殺余。

translations.literal: Yu suspected Ai would plot a change, stripped his authority; Ai was enraged; taking advantage of Yu's temple sacrifice, he killed Yu at night.
translations.idiomatic: Yu suspected Ai of plotting rebellion and stripped him of power. Enraged, Ai killed Yu one night while he was offering at the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 高宗葬以王禮，諡曰隱。

translations.literal: Gaozong buried him with princely rites; posthumous name Yin (Hidden).
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong buried him with the rites due a prince and gave him the posthumous name Yin (the Concealed).

translations.idiomatic: This biography was restored from the History of the Northern Dynasties; occasional stray phrases likely come from the Xiaoshi compiled by the Gao family."

translations.literal: "The Lü Zuo Lady of the Hall bore Prince Yu of Nan'an" — in various editions and Beishi juan 16 "zuo" (left) is written as "shi" (stone).
translations.idiomatic: Regarding "the Lü Zuo Lady of the Hall bore Prince Yu of Nan'an": various editions and Beishi juan 16 read "zuo" (left) as "shi" (stone).

translations.idiomatic: The Rouran ruler Wuti's younger sister served as Wei's Zuo Lady of the Hall and appears repeatedly in the records; "Lü" is the shortened form of the Rouran clan name Muguilü.

translations.idiomatic: "Stone" is a corruption of "zuo."

translations.literal: "Lü Zuo Lady of the Hall" should be read as a single phrase.
translations.idiomatic: "Lü Zuo Lady of the Hall" should be read as a single phrase.

translations.literal: The text is corrected accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: The text is corrected accordingly.

sentences.zh: 其小兒猫兒真虎頭龍頭並闕母氏 諸本無「真」字，北史卷一六有。

translations.literal: His younger sons Mao'er, Zhen, Hutou, and Longtou all lack their mothers' names — various editions lack the character "zhen," but Beishi juan 16 has it.
translations.idiomatic: His younger sons Mao'er, Zhen, Hutou, and Longtou all lack their mothers' names; various editions omit "zhen," but Beishi juan 16 has it.

sentences.zh: 按卷四下世祖紀下太平真君十一年二月記「皇子真薨」。

translations.literal: Compare the Taiping Zhenjun eleventh year, second month entry in juan 4b of Shizu's annals: "Prince Zhen died."
translations.idiomatic: Compare juan 4b of Shizu's annals, second month of the eleventh year of Taiping Zhenjun: "Prince Zhen died."

sentences.zh: 此傳脫去「真」字，十一男就少了一人，今據北史補。

translations.literal: This biography dropped the character "zhen"; the eleven sons are thus one short; it is restored here from Beishi.
translations.idiomatic: This biography dropped "zhen," leaving one son too few among the eleven; it is restored here from Beishi.

sentences.zh: 慕利延兄子拾寅走河曲 諸本及北史卷一六「子」上無「兄」字，「河」作「阿」。

translations.literal: Muliyan's elder brother's son Shibin fled to Hequ — various editions and Beishi juan 16 lack "elder brother" before "son," and read "he" (river) as "a."
translations.idiomatic: Muliyan's elder brother's son Shibin fled to Hequ; various editions and Beishi juan 16 lack "elder brother" before "son" and read "he" (river) as "a."

translations.idiomatic: "Hequ" and "Hexi" are both acceptable; various editions read "qu," which is retained here.

translations.literal: There was the house of Rong Hu — compare Jinshu juan 110, annals of Murong Jun: in the eighth year of Yonghe, "Jin General of Pacifying the North Rong Hu rebelled with Pengcheng and Lu commandery and submitted to Jun."
translations.idiomatic: There was the house of Rong Hu — compare Jinshu juan 110, annals of Murong Jun: in Yonghe year 8, "Jin General of Pacifying the North Rong Hu rebelled with Pengcheng and Lu commandery and submitted to Jun."

sentences.zh: 令制百家為黨族二十家為閭五家為比隣百家之內有帥二十五 按百家之內，二十家為閭，應有閭長五人；

translations.idiomatic: The statute made a hundred households a dangzu, twenty a lü, and five a bilin; within a hundred households there were to be twenty-five leaders — with twenty households per lü there should be five lü heads;

sentences.zh: 五家為比隣，應有隣長二十人，合計已達「有帥二十五」之數，再加黨族之長，就有二十六人，數目不符。

translations.literal: five households make a bilin, so there should be twenty bilin heads, totaling twenty-five leaders already; adding the dangzu head makes twenty-six, which does not match the number.
translations.idiomatic: and five households per bilin should yield twenty bilin heads, already reaching "twenty-five leaders"; adding the dangzu head makes twenty-six, which does not match.

sentences.zh: 疑當作「二十五家為閭」，則閭長四人，正合二十五之數。

translations.literal: It should read "twenty-five households make a lü"; then four lü heads would exactly make twenty-five.
translations.idiomatic: It should read "twenty-five households make a lü"; then four lü heads would exactly make twenty-five.

sentences.zh: 孝友在尹積年 北、汲、殿、局四本「尹」作「郡」，百衲本的底本和南本作「尹」，百衲本已從他本改。

translations.literal: Xiaoyou served many years as Intendant — the Bei, Ji, Dian, and Ju editions read "jun" (commandery) for "yin" (Intendant); the Baibaina base and Nan editions read "yin," and the Baibaina was already changed from other editions.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyou served many years as Intendant; the Bei, Ji, Dian, and Ju editions read "commandery" for "Intendant"; the Baibaina base and Nan editions read "Intendant," and the Baibaina was already changed from other editions.

sentences.zh: 按北史卷一六、北齊書卷二八元孝友傳也作「尹」。

translations.literal: Beishi juan 16 and Beiqishu juan 28, Yuan Xiaoyou's biography, also read "yin."
translations.idiomatic: Beishi juan 16 and Beiqishu juan 28, Yuan Xiaoyou's biography, also read "yin."

sentences.zh: 孝友當是魏尹，北史刪略，致此「尹」字沒有着落。

translations.literal: Xiaoyou must have been Intendant of the Capital; Beishi abbreviates, leaving this "yin" without a clear referent.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyou must have been Intendant of the Capital; Beishi abbreviates, leaving this "yin" without a clear referent.

sentences.zh: 後人遂臆改為「郡」，其實上面也不云孝友曾為某郡太守，仍然沒有着落。

translations.literal: Later men therefore guessed and changed it to "commandery," yet the text above does not say Xiaoyou ever served as administrator of any commandery, so it still lacks a referent.
translations.idiomatic: Later editors guessed and changed it to "commandery," yet the text above never says Xiaoyou served as administrator of any commandery, so it still lacks a referent.

sentences.zh: 百衲本的底本和南本不誤，今從之。

translations.literal: The Baibaina base and Nan editions are not in error; the correction follows them.
translations.idiomatic: The Baibaina base and Nan editions are correct; the text follows them.

sentences.zh: 今北鎮諸將舊常云一人代外邏 按此句不甚可解。

translations.literal: Now the northern garrison generals long customarily said one man deputizes for outer patrol — this sentence is hard to understand.
translations.idiomatic: Regarding "now the northern garrison generals long customarily said one man deputizes for outer patrol" — this sentence is hard to understand.

sentences.zh: 「云」即「雲」，疑本作「舊常一人雲、代外邏」。

translations.literal: "Said" is "yun" (cloud/say); the original likely read "long customarily one man Yun-Dai outer patrol."
translations.idiomatic: "Said" is "yun"; the original likely read "long customarily one man Yun-Dai outer patrol."

sentences.zh: 「雲代」指雲中、代京。

translations.literal: "Yun-Dai" refers to Yunzhong and Daijing.
translations.idiomatic: "Yun-Dai" refers to Yunzhong and Daijing.

sentences.zh: 傳本誤倒，「雲」寫作「云」，遂不可通。

translations.literal: The transmitted text was inverted by error; "yun" was written as "cloud," and the passage became unintelligible.
translations.idiomatic: The transmitted text was inverted in error; "yun" was written as the homophone "cloud," and the passage became unintelligible.

sentences.zh: 又孟都潘紹等數百人皆叩頭就法 按上文見張孟都、馬潘、張叔緒，疑「紹」字乃「緒」之訛，「叔緒」單稱「緒」。

translations.literal: Also Meng Du, Pan Shao, and several hundred others all knocked their heads and submitted to the law — the text above mentions Zhang Meng Du, Ma Pan, and Zhang Shuxu; "shao" is likely a corruption of "xu," with "Shuxu" abbreviated as "xu."
translations.idiomatic: Also Meng Du, Pan Shao, and several hundred others all knocked their heads and submitted to the law; the text above mentions Zhang Meng Du, Ma Pan, and Zhang Shuxu; "shao" is likely a corruption of "xu," with "Shuxu" abbreviated as "xu."

sentences.zh: 榮平 諸本及北史卷一六「平」作「卒」，獨殿本作「平」。

translations.literal: Rong Ping — various editions and Beishi juan 16 read "zu" (die) for "ping"; only the Dian edition reads "ping."
translations.idiomatic: Rong Ping — various editions and Beishi juan 16 read "died" for "ping"; only the Dian edition reads "ping."

sentences.zh: 按葛榮被擒就法，過去史籍不可能稱之為「卒」，今從殿本。

translations.literal: Ge Rong was captured and executed by law; past histories could not have called him "died"; the Dian edition is followed.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Rong was captured and executed; past histories could not have called him "died"; the Dian edition is followed.

sentences.zh: 廣陽王建 諸本「建」下有「閭」字。

translations.literal: Guangyang Wang Jian — various editions have the character "Lü" after "jian."
translations.idiomatic: Guangyang Wang Jian — various editions have the character "Lü" after "jian."

sentences.zh: 按這是後人誤讀傳序，把「閭左昭儀」的「閭」字和上「建」字連讀，以為廣陽王名「建閭」，這裏又妄增「閭」字。

translations.literal: Later men misread the preface and joined the "Lü" of "Lü Zuo Lady of the Hall" with the preceding "jian," thinking the Guangyang prince was named "Jianlü"; the spurious "Lü" was added here.
translations.idiomatic: Later readers misread the preface and joined the "Lü" of "Lü Zuo Lady of the Hall" with "jian," inventing the name "Jianlü" for the Guangyang prince; the spurious "Lü" was added here.

sentences.zh: 今據冊府卷二八四

translations.literal: It is deleted here according to Cefu yuangui juan 284
translations.idiomatic: Deleted here according to Cefu yuangui juan 284

sentences.zh: 〈三三四六頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 3346〉

sentences.zh: 、北史卷一六刪。

translations.literal: and Beishi juan 16.
translations.idiomatic: and Beishi juan 16.

sentences.zh: 子深 按魏書紀傳都作「廣陽王淵」。

translations.literal: Son Shen — the Wei annals and biographies all write "Guangyang Wang Yuan."
translations.idiomatic: Son Shen — the Wei annals and biographies all write "Guangyang Wang Yuan."

sentences.zh: 此傳以北史補，北史避唐諱，改「淵」作「深」。

translations.literal: This biography was supplemented from Beishi; Beishi avoids Tang taboo and changes "Yuan" to "Shen."
translations.idiomatic: This biography was supplemented from Beishi; Beishi avoids Tang taboo and changes "Yuan" to "Shen."

sentences.zh: 詔深為北道大都督 按卷九肅宗紀正光五年五月：「詔尚書令李崇為大都督，率廣陽王淵等北討。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Shen Grand Commander of the Northern Route — compare juan 9, Suzong's annals, fifth month of Zhengguang year 5: "An edict appointed Minister of State Li Chong Grand Commander, leading Guangyang Wang Yuan and others on a northern campaign."
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Shen Grand Commander of the Northern Route — compare juan 9, Suzong's annals, fifth month of Zhengguang year 5: "An edict appointed Minister of State Li Chong Grand Commander, leading Guangyang Wang Yuan and others on a northern campaign."

sentences.zh: 」當時李崇是大都督，元淵受他節度，不得有「大都督」之號，下文崔暹只稱東道都督，可證。

translations.literal: At that time Li Chong was Grand Commander; Yuan could not have held the title of Grand Commander under him; below, Cui Xuan is called only Eastern Route Commander, which confirms this.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Chong was Grand Commander; Yuan could not have held the title Grand Commander under him; below, Cui Xuan is called only Eastern Route Commander, which confirms this.

sentences.zh: 這裏「大」字衍。

translations.literal: The character "da" (grand) here is spurious.
translations.idiomatic: The character "grand" here is spurious.

sentences.zh: 時東道都督崔暹敗於白道 北史卷一六，冊府卷四０四

translations.literal: At that time Eastern Route Commander Cui Xuan was defeated at Baidao — Beishi juan 16 and Cefu juan 404
translations.idiomatic: At that time Eastern Route Commander Cui Xuan was defeated at Baidao — Beishi juan 16 and Cefu juan 404

sentences.zh: 〈四八０八頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 4808〉

sentences.zh: 此下有「深率諸軍退還朔州」一句，此傳脫。

translations.literal: have after this the sentence "Shen led the armies in retreat to Shuozhou"; this biography omits it.
translations.idiomatic: have after this the sentence "Shen led the armies in retreat to Shuozhou"; this biography omits it.

sentences.zh: 敢為逆命 諸本及北史卷一六無「敢」字，據冊府卷四０四

translations.literal: Dared to take treasonous command — various editions and Beishi juan 16 lack "dared"; restored from Cefu juan 404
translations.idiomatic: Dared to take treasonous command — various editions and Beishi juan 16 lack "dared"; restored from Cefu juan 404

sentences.zh: 〈四八０八頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 4808〉

sentences.zh: 補。

translations.literal: Supplemented.
translations.idiomatic: Restored here.

sentences.zh: 詔遣黃門郎楊昱分散之於冀定瀛三州就食 諸本及北史卷一六「昱」作「置」。

translations.literal: An edict sent Palace Attendant Yang Yu to disperse them among Ji, Ding, and Ying provinces for subsistence — various editions and Beishi juan 16 read "zhi" (place) for "Yu."
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent Palace Attendant Yang Yu to disperse them among Ji, Ding, and Ying provinces for subsistence; various editions and Beishi juan 16 read "place" for "Yu."

sentences.zh: 按事見卷五八楊昱傳，「置」字訛，今改正。

translations.literal: The matter appears in juan 58, Yang Yu's biography; "zhi" is a corruption and is corrected here.
translations.idiomatic: The matter appears in juan 58, Yang Yu's biography; "place" is a corruption and is corrected here.

sentences.zh: 戰敗於白牛邏 諸本及北史卷一六「邏」都作「還」。

translations.literal: Defeated at Bainiu Luo — various editions and Beishi juan 16 read "huan" (return) for "luo."
translations.idiomatic: Defeated at Bainiu Luo — various editions and Beishi juan 16 read "return" for "luo."

sentences.zh: 按元融敗於白牛邏，歷見卷九肅宗紀孝昌二年九月辛亥條和卷一九下融本傳。

translations.literal: Yuan Rong was defeated at Bainiu Luo, as repeatedly recorded in juan 9, Suzong's annals, ninth month of Xiaochang year 2, and juan 19b, Rong's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Rong was defeated at Bainiu Luo, as repeatedly recorded in juan 9, Suzong's annals, ninth month of Xiaochang year 2, and juan 19b, Rong's biography.

sentences.zh: 「還」字訛，今改正。

translations.literal: "Return" is a corruption and is corrected here.
translations.idiomatic: "Return" is a corruption and is corrected here.

sentences.zh: 子湛字士深 諸本及北史卷一六「深」都作「淵」，墓誌集釋元湛墓誌

translations.literal: Son Zhan, styled Shishen — various editions and Beishi juan 16 read "shen" as "yuan"; the collected epitaphs, Yuan Zhan's epitaph
translations.idiomatic: Son Zhan, styled Shishen — various editions and Beishi juan 16 read "shen" as "yuan"; the collected epitaphs, Yuan Zhan's epitaph

sentences.zh: 〈圖版九六〉

translations.literal: 〈plate 96〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈plate 96〉

sentences.zh: 作「字士深」。

translations.literal: reads "styled Shishen."
translations.idiomatic: reads "styled Shishen."

sentences.zh: 按父名「淵」，子不可能以「淵」為字。

translations.literal: The father's name was Yuan; the son could not take Yuan as his style.
translations.idiomatic: The father's name was Yuan; the son could not take Yuan as his style.

sentences.zh: 又北史例避唐諱，何故於其父則改「淵」為「深」，於子則直書不諱？

translations.literal: Moreover, Beishi routinely avoids Tang taboo — why change the father's "Yuan" to "Shen" yet write the son's name without taboo?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Beishi routinely avoids Tang taboo — why change the father's "Yuan" to "Shen" yet write the son's name without taboo?

sentences.zh: 顯然這裏本作「士深」，後人不知「元深」之「深」本是「淵」字，反疑這裏「士深」為北史諱改，實是適得其反。

translations.literal: Clearly the original here read "Shishen"; later men, not knowing that Yuan Shen's "shen" was originally "yuan," instead suspected "Shishen" was Beishi's taboo alteration — the opposite of the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Clearly the original here read "Shishen"; later readers, not knowing that Yuan Shen's "shen" was originally "yuan," suspected "Shishen" was Beishi's taboo alteration — the opposite of the truth.

sentences.zh: 今據墓誌回改。

translations.literal: The text is reverted here according to the epitaph.
translations.idiomatic: The text is reverted here according to the epitaph.
